# agentic-sdd (full)

> Spec-Driven Development that finishes: one skill that drives GitHub Spec Kit end to end on Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, and Grok Build, runs pstack inside every phase, and closes a feature only on REA runtime evidence. One converge per spec; small specs; seven harness layers probed per host.

Every file listed in llms.txt, inlined. Generated by scripts/build_llms.py.


---

<!-- file: README.md -->

# agentic-sdd

Spec-Driven Development that finishes. One skill that drives
[GitHub Spec Kit](https://github.com/github/spec-kit) end to end on
**Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, and Grok Build**, runs
[pstack](https://github.com/cursor/plugins/tree/main/pstack) inside every phase
for rigor, and refuses to call a feature done without
[REA](https://github.com/morluto/rea) runtime evidence.

```text
specify → plan → tasks → implement → converge (once) → REA closeout → next spec
```

| Layer | Owner | What it contributes |
|---|---|---|
| Phase order and artifacts | Spec Kit | `.specify/`, `specs/NNN-*/{spec,plan,tasks,converge}.md` |
| Goal, contracts, continuity | agentic-sdd | Final Goal pinning, phase contracts, `progress.md` breadcrumbs, recovery, one converge per spec, small specs |
| How a phase executes | pstack | `sharpen`/`how` on entry, `architect`/`arena` at plan, poteto non-negotiables and `poteto-agent` leaves at implement, `blast-radius` + `no-comments` + `interrogate` at converge |
| Proof | REA | `capture_process_scenario` and friends; a feature closes on an Evidence id, not a claim |
| Resilience | seven harness layers | workspace facts, procedure, source access, action rules, reviewer evidence, effort, completion goal, probed per host by `scripts/harness_probe.py` |

Unattended by default: `/agentic-sdd` advances every phase and every remaining
numbered feature without a phase quiz. It asks once only at hard boundaries
(destructive operations, secrets, scope beyond the Final Goal, plugin installs).

## Quick start

Requirements: Python 3.11+, Node 20+ (for `npx` and REA), `uv` (for the Spec
Kit CLI), `git`, and at least one of the four host CLIs. `bun` is needed only
by pstack's own playbook checker. Anything missing that Homebrew can install is
part of the plan the installer shows you.

### Agent mode (recommended)

Open Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, or Grok Build on your machine and paste this.
The agent reads the docs, inspects your machine, shows you the plan, and asks
once before changing anything.

```text
Install agentic-sdd on this machine.
1. Read https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jonsoku-dev/agentic-sdd/main/llms.txt and the README it links.
2. Clone https://github.com/jonsoku-dev/agentic-sdd to ~/.agents/skills/agentic-sdd (git pull if it already exists).
3. Run ~/.agents/skills/agentic-sdd/install.sh --dry-run and show me the detected state and the full plan, including the manual items.
4. Ask me once whether to proceed. Only on yes, run ~/.agents/skills/agentic-sdd/install.sh --yes.
5. Show me the verify output, what I must restart, and what I must do inside an IDE. Change nothing the plan did not list.
```

### Manual mode

```sh
git clone https://github.com/jonsoku-dev/agentic-sdd ~/.agents/skills/agentic-sdd
~/.agents/skills/agentic-sdd/install.sh
```

Either way the work is done by `install.sh`, which with no flags runs
`scripts/setup.py`:

1. **detects** which hosts are on this machine (`claude`, `codex`, `agent`/`~/.cursor`,
   `grok`), which prerequisites exist (`uv`, `node`, `bun`, `gh`, Homebrew),
   what pstack, Spec Kit, and REA versions are installed, which MCP entries,
   mandates, hooks, links, and model sheets are already in place;
2. **prints the plan**: every command it is about to run, in order, plus the
   few things only you can do (install pstack in the Cursor IDE, run
   `/setup-pstack` once per host to pin models);
3. **asks once** (`Proceed? [y/N]`), then applies: Homebrew prerequisites,
   the Spec Kit CLI, pstack on Claude Code / Codex / Grok through the
   `pstack-claude` marketplace, REA MCP registration via `rea setup --client`,
   the skill symlinks, the Codex `AGENTS.md` mandate block, the Grok home rule
   and agent links, the Cursor Agent CLI skill links and `sdd-continue` hook;
4. **verifies** with `deps.py check` and the harness probe for each host and
   tells you what to restart.

It touches only hosts it found, writes only marked blocks and named entries in
files you own, and is idempotent: rerun it after a `git pull` or whenever the
plan shows something missing.

```sh
./install.sh --dry-run        # detect and plan, change nothing
./install.sh --yes            # no prompt (CI, dotfiles)
./install.sh --check-deps     # later: what is behind, with the update command per row
./install.sh --deps           # update everything that can be updated unattended
./install.sh --link-only      # only the symlinks (the old default)
```

Every host-specific step is also available as its own flag (listed in each
host section and in `./install.sh --help`) for people who prefer to apply them
one at a time.

Then, in a repository that already has Spec Kit (`specify init` is the
`setup-speckit-multi-agent` skill's job, not this one):

```sh
~/.agents/skills/agentic-sdd/install.sh --project /path/to/repo   # project playbook (pstack port) + Cursor rule
python3 ~/.agents/skills/agentic-sdd/scripts/harness_probe.py --host claude --project /path/to/repo
```

The probe prints the pstack version it found, missing core skills, the model
sheet, one `ok`/`gap` line per harness layer, and two breadcrumb lines to paste
into `progress.md`. Start the run by asking the host for the Final Goal in
plain words, or type the skill's name (`/agentic-sdd`, `$agentic-sdd`,
`/skill agentic-sdd` depending on the host).

## How a run looks

1. **Enter.** Resolve the nearest `.specify/`, the active numbered feature, and
   its phase from the artifacts and `progress.md`. Load
   `references/pstack-integration.md` and `references/harness-layers.md`, run
   the probe, record the breadcrumbs. `O-sharpen` pins the Final Goal and the
   acceptance criteria; nobody is quizzed.
2. **Specify, plan, tasks.** Spec Kit commands write the artifacts; the
   obligations run beside them: `technical-writing` + `unslop` on the spec,
   `how` for brownfield evidence, `architect` (or `arena` when shapes compete)
   when code crosses a function boundary, `principle-sequence-verifiable-units`
   so every task ends in a check. Tasks beyond about twelve mean a smaller spec.
3. **Implement.** The host's poteto agent takes one admitted task packet at a
   time, in its own worktree, with the model and effort the pstack sheet names.
   The lead reviews every diff and never claims a dispatch it did not observe.
4. **Converge, once.** `blast-radius`, `no-comments`, then a two-to-four model
   `interrogate` panel. Act-on findings are appended to `tasks.md` and
   implemented in one bounded fix round. There is no second converge: gaps
   that survive become the next, smaller spec (`closed-carryover`).
5. **REA closeout.** Run the real artifact under REA and record the Evidence
   id in `converge.md` and `progress.md`. Disposition is `pass`,
   `not-applicable`, or `blocked-limitation`; only `pass` closes the feature.
6. **Next spec or stop.** `progress.md` ends with `Final Goal status` and a
   `Next action` line a cold session can resume from.

Every obligation leaves one line in `progress.md`, for example
`pstack: O-interrogate|claude|2x pstack:effort-low (opus, haiku) -> 1 act-on -> T004 appended`,
plus `ROUTING:` lines that record requested versus observed model and effort.
The full phase → obligation map is in `references/pstack-integration.md`.

## Claude Code

`install.sh` does all of this when it finds `claude`. The manual equivalents:

**Install pstack** (the `pstack-claude` port of the Cursor plugin):

```sh
claude plugin marketplace add michael-denyer/pstack-claude
claude plugin install pstack@pstack-claude --scope user
```

**What this skill adds.** Nothing beyond the symlink is required: the plugin's
`SessionStart` hook injects the poteto-mode mandate ("invoke `pstack:poteto-mode`
for multi-file, design, or unknown-cause work"), and `/agentic-sdd` satisfies
that mandate from inside the Spec Kit phases instead of opening a free-standing
playbook. The project playbook from `install.sh --project` anchors three
handoffs on the port's Feature and Bug fix steps so a plain request in a Spec
Kit repo still resolves the phase first.

**Dispatch.** Implement leaves are `subagent_type: "pstack:poteto-agent"`, or
`pstack:poteto-agent-<level>` when the sheet names an effort. Review panels use
`pstack:effort-<level>` with the `model` family (`opus`, `fable`, `sonnet`,
`haiku`) from `~/.claude/pstack-models.md`, written by `/pstack:setup-pstack`.
Delegates run in their own worktree.

**Completion.** `/goal` is Claude Code's own stop-hook goal; agentic-sdd's
Final Goal in `progress.md` is the durable copy a resumed session reads.

**Headless.** `claude -p --output-format stream-json --verbose --dangerously-skip-permissions "<Final Goal>"`
exposes every `Skill` and `Agent` call for measurement.

**Known limits.** A plugin update needs a Claude Code restart to load; the
sandbox has no `CLAUDE.md`, so the probe reports L1 as a gap until you add one.

## Codex

`install.sh` does all of this when it finds `codex`. The manual equivalents:

**Install pstack:**

```sh
codex plugin marketplace add michael-denyer/pstack-claude
codex plugin add pstack@pstack-claude
# ~/.codex/config.toml: [features] multi_agent = true   (spawn_agent)
~/.agents/skills/agentic-sdd/install.sh --codex-mandate
```

**Why `--codex-mandate` exists.** Codex runs a plugin's `SessionStart` hook
only after you trust it in `/hooks`, and `codex exec` never trusts hooks. So
the mandate text goes into `~/.codex/AGENTS.md` between
`<!-- pstack-mandate:start -->` and `<!-- pstack-mandate:end -->`; the installer
writes and replaces that block only.

**Dispatch.** `spawn_agent` with instructions to read `poteto-mode/SKILL.md`
first. Pass `model` as a slug the tool actually lists; omitting it makes the
host inject the parent slug, which a ChatGPT account may reject
(`gpt-6.1-sol` on the machine this was built on). Effort goes through
`reasoning_effort`. The sheet is `~/.codex/pstack-models.md`; the one shipped
in the evals pins every role to `gpt-6-luna` and forbids `gpt-5.6-*`.

**Breadcrumbs.** Write the line form (`pstack: …`, `ROUTING: …`) at column 1.
Codex tends to write prose bullets instead, and the probe and the eval
measurers only count the line form.

**Headless.** `codex exec --json --skip-git-repo-check -m gpt-6-luna --dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox "<Final Goal>" < /dev/null`.
`--full-auto` does not exist in codex-cli 0.162; the stdin redirect matters
when the command runs in the background.

**Known limits.** Codex may rewrite `config.toml` (`model`, reasoning effort)
during a session; check it after a run that behaved unexpectedly.

## Cursor

`install.sh` does everything below except the IDE plugin install, which Cursor only offers inside the editor. The manual equivalents:

**Install pstack** from the IDE: `/add-plugin pstack` (official plugin by
Lauren Tan). Then:

```sh
~/.agents/skills/agentic-sdd/install.sh --project /path/to/repo   # writes .cursor/rules/agentic-sdd.mdc
~/.agents/skills/agentic-sdd/install.sh --apply-cursor-hooks      # sdd-continue stop hook (dated backup of ~/.cursor/hooks.json)
~/.agents/skills/agentic-sdd/install.sh --cursor-cli-skills       # expose the plugin's skills to the Cursor Agent CLI
```

**Why Cursor needs the rule.** The official plugin has no hooks, no project
playbooks, and marks `poteto-mode` `disable-model-invocation: true`: the model
cannot open it on its own, only you can with `/poteto-mode`. Without a project
rule the Agent CLI routed bug and design prompts to whatever other skill packs
were installed. `.cursor/rules/agentic-sdd.mdc` (always applied) carries the
same three Spec Kit handoffs as the project playbook, plus a one-file exemption
so a typo fix does not open the whole cycle. The skill reads
`poteto-mode/SKILL.md` as a reference for the non-negotiables instead of
invoking it.

**Dispatch.** Native `subagent_type: "poteto-agent"` (the plugin's agent,
`is_background: true`). Model lines come from
`~/.cursor/rules/pstack-models.mdc` when `/setup-pstack` wrote one. When the
account's usage limit blocks a non-default model seat, the lead implements the
leaf itself and records `observed: unavailable|usage-limit`; review seats are
recorded as `inherit`.

**Continuation.** The `sdd-continue` stop hook re-prompts the agent with the
`Next action` line from `progress.md` until the Final Goal is met
(`references/cursor-continuation.md`).

**Headless.** `agent -p --output-format stream-json --force "<Final Goal>"`.
Plan-shaped prompts can switch the agent into Cursor's plan mode, which a
headless run cannot answer.

**Known limits.** The plugin cache path
`~/.cursor/plugins/cache/cursor-public/pstack/<hash>/` changes on every plugin
update, which silently breaks the `~/.cursor/skills` links; rerun
`install.sh --cursor-cli-skills` (it prunes the dead links first).

## Grok Build

`install.sh` does all of this when it finds `grok`. The manual equivalents:

**Install pstack** (the same port, through Grok's marketplace; Grok can also
read the Claude plugin cache through `[compat.claude]`):

```sh
grok plugin marketplace add michael-denyer/pstack-claude
grok plugin install pstack@pstack-claude --trust
~/.agents/skills/agentic-sdd/install.sh --grok-mandate --grok-agents
```

**Why the two flags exist.** Grok runs `SessionStart` hooks but never injects
their stdout, so `--grok-mandate` writes the mandate plus the three Spec Kit
handoffs as a home rule, `~/.grok/rules/pstack-mandate.md`, which Grok always
loads. Plugin agents are not in the `spawn_subagent` enum, so `--grok-agents`
links the port's `poteto-agent.md` and `comment-sicko.md` into
`~/.grok/agents/`, where they are.

**Dispatch.** `spawn_subagent` with `subagent_type: "poteto-agent"`; the
subagent reads `poteto-mode/SKILL.md` before working. `[subagents.models]` in
`~/.grok/config.toml` pins a model when you want one; without a sheet the
`ROUTING:` lines read `model unpinned, observed unknown`.

**MCP.** Grok loads `~/.cursor/mcp.json` through `[compat.cursor]`, so REA
configured for Cursor is already visible to Grok.

**Headless.** `grok --output-format json --always-approve -p "<Final Goal>" < /dev/null`.
Put `-p` last: `grok -p --output-format json` reads `--output-format` as the
prompt.

**Known limits.** Grok is the slowest host on the same brief (roughly four
times Claude's wall time on the three-spec eval) because every spec pays the
full phase overhead and the context grows to ~180k tokens; keep its specs
small.

## Keeping dependencies current

```sh
./install.sh --check-deps              # table: installed vs latest; exit 1 when anything is behind
./install.sh --deps                    # update unattended, then relink mandates, agents, and skill links
python3 scripts/deps.py update --yes --hosts   # also run claude/codex/grok/agent self-update
python3 scripts/deps.py check --json   # machine-readable
```

| Component | How it is read | How it is updated |
|---|---|---|
| Spec Kit CLI (`specify`) | `uv tool list` | `uv tool install --force --from git+https://github.com/github/spec-kit.git specify-cli` |
| pstack on Claude Code | plugin cache manifest | `claude plugin marketplace update pstack-claude && claude plugin update pstack@pstack-claude` (restart to load) |
| pstack on Codex | plugin cache manifest | `codex plugin marketplace upgrade && codex plugin add pstack@pstack-claude` |
| pstack on Grok | installed-plugins manifest | `grok plugin marketplace update pstack-claude && grok plugin update` |
| pstack on Cursor | plugin cache manifest | IDE only; reported, then `--cursor-cli-skills` relinks |
| `rea-agents` pins | every host MCP config (`~/.claude.json`, `~/.cursor/mcp.json`, `~/.codex/config.toml`, `~/.grok/config.toml`, Claude desktop, Antigravity, Hermes) | pins rewritten to the npm latest with a `.bak-rea-<version>` copy, npx cache warmed; restart hosts so MCP servers respawn |
| Host CLIs | `--version` | `claude update`, `codex update`, `grok update`, `agent update` (only with `--hosts`) |

Pin REA at **6.7.0 or newer**: older releases fail every process capture whenever
an unrelated restricted process (a browser renderer) starts mid-capture.

## Uninstall

`install.sh` only ever creates symlinks, a few files it owns, and marked blocks
inside files you own. Uninstall is the exact inverse.

```sh
~/.agents/skills/agentic-sdd/install.sh --uninstall                          # everything under $HOME this script created
~/.agents/skills/agentic-sdd/install.sh --uninstall --project /path/to/repo   # + the two project files
~/.agents/skills/agentic-sdd/install.sh --uninstall --purge-deps --yes        # + pstack plugins and the Spec Kit CLI
rm -rf ~/.agents/skills/agentic-sdd                                           # finally, the checkout itself
```

| Removed by `--uninstall` | Detail |
|---|---|
| Skill symlinks | `agentic-sdd` in `~/.agents/skills`, `~/.claude/skills`, `~/.codex/skills`, `~/.cursor/skills`, `~/.grok/skills` (only when they are symlinks) |
| Grok files | `~/.grok/agents/poteto-agent.md`, `~/.grok/agents/comment-sicko.md`, `~/.grok/rules/pstack-mandate.md`, `~/.grok/hooks/pstack-session-start.json` |
| Codex block | the `<!-- pstack-mandate:start … end -->` block in `~/.codex/AGENTS.md`; the rest of the file is untouched |
| Cursor CLI links | every `~/.cursor/skills/*` symlink that points into a pstack plugin cache |
| Cursor hooks | `~/.cursor/hooks/agentic-sdd-continue/` and the `agentic-sdd-continue` entries in `~/.cursor/hooks.json`; other hooks stay |
| With `--project DIR` | `DIR/.agents/playbooks/agentic-sdd.md`, `DIR/.cursor/rules/agentic-sdd.mdc`, and the directories if they became empty |
| With `--purge-deps --yes` | `claude plugin uninstall pstack@pstack-claude`, `codex plugin remove pstack`, `grok plugin uninstall pstack-*`, `uv tool uninstall specify-cli`. Cursor's plugin is removed from the IDE. Without `--yes` it only prints what it would do. |

Kept on purpose, and printed at the end of every uninstall so you can remove
them by hand:

- the `rea` MCP server entries in each host config (this script only repins
  their version; you added the servers),
- the pstack model sheets (`pstack-models.md` / `.mdc`),
- backups the script wrote (`~/.cursor/hooks.json.bak-*`, `<config>.bak-rea-<version>`),
- your projects' `.specify/`, `specs/`, and `progress.md`.

Nothing is deleted from a project except the two files above, and nothing is
deleted from a host config except the marked block and the named hook entries.

## Evidence that it works

[`docs/BENCHMARKS.md`](docs/BENCHMARKS.md) has the full picture: method,
routing table, a gate-by-gate matrix of what each host actually invoked at
every Spec Kit gate, result comparisons, and the A/B against plain Spec Kit.
`docs/evals/` keeps the records; raw headless transcripts are gitignored.

- `2026-10-19-sandbox-ab/`: Spec Kit alone versus this stack on the same brief.
  The stack caught three shipped defects, left a resumable `progress.md`, and
  cost roughly ten times as much on a 60-line feature.
- `2026-10-20-host-matrix/`: four hosts × (routing prompts, a real feature, a
  three-part goal with the split rule). All four hosts delivered the feature
  with a black-box pass, exactly one converge, and a REA Evidence id; the
  trivial prompt invoked nothing on any host; the complex goal was split into
  two or three small specs with no reconverge and no carryover. Claude $7.49
  and $12.07; Grok $7.15 and $17.65; Codex and Cursor on subscriptions.
  `result.md` lists every confound.

## Repository layout

| Path | Role |
|---|---|
| `SKILL.md` | Entrypoint the hosts load |
| `references/` | Phase contracts, pstack map, harness layers, poteto-mode anatomy, model routing, recovery, REA closeout, per-host guides |
| `scripts/` | `harness_probe.py`, `deps.py`, verification evidence and guards, criterion gate, scaffold helpers |
| `templates/playbooks/` | pstack project playbook (port hosts) |
| `templates/cursor-rules/` | Cursor project rule |
| `hosts/cursor/` | `sdd-continue` hooks and the `hooks.json` snippet |
| `install.sh` | Link, configure, update, and uninstall per host |
| `tests/` | `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -p 'test_*.py'` |
| `evals/` | Behavioral eval cases |
| `personas/` | Provider personas, loaded only when a host asks for one |
| `agents/openai.yaml` | Codex skill metadata |
| `visualizer/` | Optional Kanban over Spec Kit artifacts: `python3 visualizer/server.py --project /path/to/repo` |
| `docs/evals/` | Measured runs and their artifacts |
| `llms.txt`, `llms-full.txt` | [llms.txt](https://llmstxt.org/) index and full inline copy of the docs for agents; regenerate with `python3 scripts/build_llms.py` (the test suite fails when they are stale) |

## Versioning and releases

Semantic Versioning, driven by [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/)
on `main` and automated with [release-please](https://github.com/googleapis/release-please):

1. Commit with `feat:`, `fix:`, `docs:`, `refactor:`, `perf:` (a `!` or a
   `BREAKING CHANGE:` footer bumps the major).
2. On every push to `main`, the `release-please` workflow opens or updates a
   release pull request that bumps `version.txt`, rewrites `CHANGELOG.md`
   from the commits, and shows the next version.
3. Merging that pull request creates the git tag `vX.Y.Z` and the GitHub
   release. Nothing is published to a package registry; a release is the tag
   plus the changelog section.

The `ci` workflow runs shell syntax checks, the unit tests, and the
`llms.txt` freshness check on every push and pull request. Current version:
`version.txt`; history: `CHANGELOG.md`.

their machine.

<!-- file: SKILL.md -->

---
name: agentic-sdd
description: >
  Coordinate or resume GitHub Spec Kit delivery through the user's Final Goal,
  unattended end-to-end by default (no phase quiz), with phase contracts, scoped
  verification, collaborative recovery, pstack-sheet model/effort routing,
  pstack execution style when available (Cursor plugin; pstack-claude port on
  Claude Code, Codex, and Grok Build),
  and a mandatory REA reverse-engineering closeout (install REA if missing).
  Default is full Spec Kit (specify → plan → tasks → implement → converge → REA),
  not light-first. Use for numbered feature cycles and SDD phase handoffs on
  Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, and Grok Build. Preserve read-only scope for
  audits and planning. Repository setup belongs to setup-speckit-multi-agent.
---

# Agentic SDD

Finish the user's original **Final Goal** with **Spec Kit as the default**.
Light scaffolding is opt-in for trivial work only — never the default.

The primary owns scope, integration, and completion. Reviewer agreement and
model scores never replace required evidence or authorization.

**Invocation of this skill for delivery/repair is a full-autonomy grant** inside
the admitted Final Goal: advance every Spec Kit phase and remaining numbered
features without a human phase quiz. See [pstack integration](references/pstack-integration.md)
for autonomy rules and phase→execution mapping.

## Host bootstrap (required)

Detect the host once, then follow that host's invocation surface. Do not invent
a second spec store. Setup/init belongs to `setup-speckit-multi-agent`.

| Host | Skill load | Spec Kit surface | Persist handoff |
|------|------------|------------------|-----------------|
| **Claude Code** | `~/.claude/skills/agentic-sdd` or project `.claude/skills/` | `/speckit.*` (or installed skill syntax) | `CLAUDE.md` + feature artifacts + `progress.md` |
| **Codex** | `~/.codex/skills/agentic-sdd` → shared `.agents/skills` | `$speckit-*` | `AGENTS.md` + feature artifacts |
| **Cursor** | `~/.cursor/skills/agentic-sdd` → shared `.agents/skills` | `/speckit.*` / Cursor skills | `.cursor/rules/` or `AGENTS.md` + feature artifacts. Resume via [cursor-continuation](references/cursor-continuation.md) |
| **Grok Build** | `~/.grok/skills/agentic-sdd` → shared `.agents/skills` | File-based `.specify/` + this skill (no native Spec Kit key yet) | Project instructions + feature artifacts |

For **greenfield vs brownfield** procedures on Claude / Codex / Cursor (human +
agent), load [host guide](references/host-guide-greenfield-brownfield.md) once
per feature when field type or host is unclear.

Read [starting-tool considerations](references/starting-tool-considerations.md)
and [agent compatibility](references/agent-compatibility.md) when the host or
invocation syntax is unclear.

Universal first actions on every host:

1. Resolve project (nearest `.specify/`), active feature, phase, revision/dirty owners.
2. Prefer read-only `setup-speckit-multi-agent` `inspect` / `sdd` when available.
3. Use installed Spec Kit phase commands — do not re-implement phases in chat.
4. Update feature artifacts and a root `progress.md` at every meaningful stage.
5. Compact only after flushing durable state (see [compaction](references/compaction-timing.md)).
6. Load [pstack integration](references/pstack-integration.md) and [harness layers](references/harness-layers.md) once per feature (or on host change); run `python scripts/harness_probe.py --host <host> --project .` and record its two breadcrumbs in `progress.md`; apply the phase→obligation map for every phase entered.
7. While a host goal (`/goal` on Claude, Cursor, Grok) is active, echo each check command and its decisive output line into the conversation after every verification; the evaluator reads the transcript, not files.

## Establish the working contract

1. Identify mode: delivery, repair, assessment, or read-only review.
   An investigation or plan is not permission to implement. Use installed project
   commands; do not initialize, upgrade, or install extensions just to run a phase.
2. Resolve the project and active feature from Spec Kit metadata, nearest
   instructions, and constitution. Record revision (if Git), dirty/untracked
   ownership, feature directory, canonical spec root (`specs/` or
   `.specify/specs/`), and phase. One writer per checkout.
3. Pin the Final Goal and verification contract in existing feature artifacts:
   acceptance conditions, admitted paths, required checks, non-goals.
   Use repository mandatory checks plus the narrowest additional proof.
   Do not add a generic verification framework by default.

Read [Spec Kit alignment](references/spec-kit-alignment.md) for project/feature
resolution, installed overrides, command syntax, or non-SDD entry points.

## Default workflow (Spec Kit)

```text
specify → plan → tasks → implement → converge → REA closeout
```

Add `clarify`, checklist, and `analyze` when ambiguity/risk warrants it or the
repository requires them. Preserve already admitted gates. Never silently
self-approve reviewer-owned checklists.

**REA closeout is mandatory** after a clean converge (and before Final Goal
finish). If REA CLI/MCP is missing, install and wire it, then analyze. See
[REA closeout](references/rea-closeout.md).

Read [phase contracts](references/phase-contract.md) when entering a phase or
handing off. Read [pstack integration](references/pstack-integration.md) for
*how* to execute inside each phase (Cursor pstack skills vs host fallbacks).

### Unattended continuity

- Do not ask which Spec Kit phase to run next. After a phase succeeds, enter the
  next unfinished admitted phase in the same turn.
- Do not end a turn only to report progress. After a commit, test, or artifact
  write, start the next unfinished admitted task in the same turn. A host notice
  about one finished subagent or shell resumes the parent Final Goal after that
  notice's follow-up. Flush `progress.md` instead of a long chat report.
- Preference or approach forks solvable by repository evidence, a prototype, or
  constitution defaults: decide, record the default in `progress.md`, continue.
  Do not offer shorthand tokens for the human to type back.
- When the feature is complete and the Final Goal still has admitted work,
  specify the next numbered feature and continue without a human phase quiz.
- **Keep specs small.** Prefer several short numbered specs over one long one.
  Split before `implement` when `tasks.md` exceeds about 12 tasks or the work
  would span more than two compactions (`O-sequence`). A `closed-carryover`
  feature's gaps become the next spec's scope; the Final Goal stays open until
  the last spec reaches REA `pass`.

### Advance, recover, finish

- Carry out admitted tasks, then run the agreed checks. Clear in-scope failure →
  fix and rerun the affected check. Missing obtainable receipt → obtain evidence.
- For approved CLI checks, use [verification execution](references/verification-execution.md)
  before another run.
- After two unchanged attempts of the same check without new acceptance evidence,
  a concrete defect, or a narrowed diagnosis, use
  [verification_guard.py](scripts/verification_guard.py) and a recovery progress
  checkpoint. A real repair still gets its first verification.
- On repeated failure, conflicting diagnoses, or verification-driven scope drift,
  use [collaborative recovery](references/recovery.md). Retry thresholds change
  the approach, not the Final Goal. Prefer pstack `O-fio` / `O-correct` /
  attack-the-premise style changes of method when available
  ([pstack integration](references/pstack-integration.md)).
- **One converge per spec.** `converge` runs once per numbered feature. If it
  appends gap tasks, do one `implement` round for exactly those tasks, rerun
  only the affected checks, then go to REA closeout. Never run `converge` a
  second time on the same spec. If the affected checks still fail after that
  round, mark the feature `closed-carryover`, write the remaining gaps
  (acceptance ID → defect → evidence) as the scope of the next, smaller numbered
  spec, and `specify` it. Context stays small; the gap is not lost.
- `converge` only assesses and appends missing in-scope tasks. Return to
  `implement` for fixes. Do not relax acceptance to get green. Prefer
  `/interrogate` (or `O-interrogate` fallback) plus
  [multi-perspective review](references/multi-perspective-review.md). With
  pstack present, a required review with no independent reviewer stays
  `BLOCKED: independent review`; self-review never closes it.
- Installed `speckit-converge` reporting `converged` is not finish. After a clean
  converge (no new tasks), run **REA closeout** before marking the feature closed
  or advancing. Prefer MCP `user-rea` / `rea` tools; if absent in delivery/repair
  closeout, install pinned `rea-agents` and `rea setup --yes --client <active-id>` for the
  **active** host only (`cursor`, `claude_code`, `codex`, or `grok_build`), then analyze.
  Record verbatim Evidence IDs in `progress.md` / `converge.md` (or bug `test.md`).
  Material findings: features → one bounded fix round (append tasks → `implement`
  once → rerun affected checks) → REA again, no second `converge`; a further
  material finding on the same spec carries over to the next small spec.
  Bugs → return to `fix` → `test` → REA again (do not append feature tasks unless
  the defect is new scope). Prior Evidence IDs are stale after the edit.
  Details: [REA closeout](references/rea-closeout.md).
- Before the next feature, review every acceptance condition with
  [direction keeping](references/direction-keeper.md).
- Finish only when Spec Kit evidence is current and REA disposition is `pass`
  or `not-applicable`. `blocked-limitation`, `tasks-appended`, or a missing
  record leave the Final Goal / feature open.

### Repair (bugs)

Use the installed Spec Kit bug extension when present:
`assess → fix → test` under `.specify/bugs/<slug>/`.
See [bug workflow](references/bug-workflow.md). Assessment and test are evidence;
only fix edits source. On Cursor, prefer `/tdd` when a cheap local test exists
(`O-tdd`).

## Execution style (pstack)

Spec Kit remains the process. pstack (when present) is the execution engine
inside admitted phases — not a second SDD.

| Priority | Action |
|----------|--------|
| 1 | Run the owning Spec Kit phase command / artifact contract |
| 2 | Apply the matching obligation from [pstack integration](references/pstack-integration.md) |
| 3 | On **Cursor**: official `pstack` skills (`/architect`, `/arena`, `/swarm`, `/interrogate`, poteto non-negotiables, `poteto-agent`) |
| 4 | On **Claude Code** with `pstack@pstack-claude`: same map via `/pstack:<skill>`; leaves via `pstack:poteto-agent[-<level>]` |
| 5 | On **Codex** with `pstack@pstack-claude`: skills load by name; leaves via the session spawn tool + `reasoning_effort` (port's `codex-tools.md`) |
| 6 | If pstack is absent: native Agent/Task + obligations; record `pstack: unavailable|<host>` once — do not stop Spec Kit |

Never start a free-standing `/poteto-mode` or `/pstack:poteto-mode` playbook that
reorders or replaces Spec Kit phases. Apply poteto non-negotiables *inside*
`implement` / `fix` batches only. The pstack SessionStart hook mandate on
Claude / Codex is satisfied by that `O-poteto` row, not by a second playbook.
Required rows in the phase map (`O-how`, `O-architect`, `O-hygiene`,
`O-interrogate`, `O-pause`, …) run as skill or obligation every time the phase
is entered; only common-core skills may be required on all hosts.

Long unattended or multi-phase runs: keep a decision trail
(`/show-me-your-work` or `/pstack:show-me-your-work`, or a feature-local TSV)
linked from `progress.md`.

## Route capabilities, not authority

Use [model routing](references/model-routing.md) for phase/role changes and
recovery turns. Keep the user's parent model. Child model and effort come, in
order, from the pstack sheet role line (`pstack-models.md` / `.mdc` after
`/setup-pstack`), the pstack skill defaults, then the parent model. The primary
decides from the written rules; no external advisor is consulted. A routing
decision is not proof a child actually ran. Dispatch the level as
`pstack:poteto-agent-<level>` on Claude and `reasoning_effort` on Codex.

Use native subagents when they clarify a failure or execute an independent
packet. Prefer the host poteto agent for implement leaves when pstack is
available (`poteto-agent` on Cursor; port equivalent on Claude). Leaves do not
delegate. If unavailable, do explicit self-review and record the limit — never
claim independent consensus.

## Light path (opt-in only)

Use a reduced path **only** when all are true:

- Trivial, reversible change (typo, one-line config, docs-only)
- Single clear acceptance check
- User did not ask for Spec Kit / high confidence / careful work
- No auth, payment, personal data, public API, schema, or multi-module blast radius

Then: short goal + AC in `progress.md` (or a tiny `spec.md`), implement, verify
once. If a runnable or build artifact exists, REA must reach `pass` (same rule as
full Spec Kit). Use `not-applicable` only when no such artifact exists. Prefer
full Spec Kit whenever unsure.

## Kanban (optional)

```sh
python /path/to/agentic-sdd/visualizer/server.py --project /path/to/repo
```

See [kanban board](references/kanban-board.md).

## Hard boundaries

Require explicit confirmation before:

- Destructive operations (delete data, drop tables, force push, etc.)
- Handling secrets or credentials
- Changing scope beyond the agreed Final Goal
- Installing Spec Kit extensions/presets/integrations

**Authorized without extra confirmation (narrow):** in delivery/repair closeout
only, when MCP and `rea` are both missing or this host’s MCP registration is
missing/stale: `npm install -g rea-agents@6.7.0` (do not upgrade a working CLI)
and `rea setup --yes --client <active-id>` for that host only
(`cursor` | `claude_code` | `codex` | `grok_build`). No `curl | bash`, no
`--all-detected`, no install from read-only/plan/audit modes.

This skill grants no permission to push, merge, deploy, stash, reset, or
force-refresh. Use `setup-speckit-multi-agent` `commit-phase` only within
already authorized scope after its gates pass.

## References

Load only when needed — see [references/INDEX.md](references/INDEX.md).

Core: `spec-kit-alignment`, `phase-contract`, `pstack-integration`,
`host-guide-greenfield-brownfield`, `verification-execution`, `recovery`,
`direction-keeper`, `model-routing`, `starting-tool-considerations`,
`agent-compatibility`, `rea-closeout`, `poteto-mode-anatomy` (how each host
reaches poteto-mode), `cursor-continuation` (Cursor only).

<!-- file: references/spec-kit-alignment.md -->

# Spec Kit alignment

Use installed commands and artifacts as execution authority. The public docs are
reference evidence, not permission to replace repository policy or upgrade tools.
This mapping was checked against the official documentation on 2026-09-25.

## Project, feature, and integration

- Resolve the nearest `.specify/`, including monorepo member projects. When set,
  `SPECIFY_INIT_DIR` selects the project; `SPECIFY_FEATURE_DIRECTORY` overrides
  `.specify/feature.json` for the active feature. Verify installed-version support.
- A Git branch is not the active-feature selector. Enforce branch alignment when
  the repository's Git workflow requires it, but do not invent that requirement
  for Git-free projects. Preserve revision and dirty ownership where Git exists.
- Read-only inspection can still encounter scripts that persist the feature
  pointer. With supported core scripts, use `SPECIFY_FEATURE_NO_PERSIST=1` for
  concurrent/read-only inspections and explicitly pin the correct feature.
- Discover the installed invocation surface: Codex commonly uses `$speckit-*`,
  other integrations use `/speckit.*`, `/speckit-*`, or their own skill syntax.
  These are agent invocations, not shell commands.
- For composition uncertainty, inspect `specify artifact list --json` and
  `specify artifact info ... --json` when the installed CLI supports them. Resolve
  project overrides, presets, and extensions before treating a bundled template
  as effective. Do not copy commands into an alternate spec store.

## Choose the process already admitted

- Feature delivery: specify → plan → tasks → implement → converge → REA closeout.
  Installed `speckit-converge` reporting converged is not finish; only REA
  disposition `pass` or `not-applicable` finishes. Add clarify, requirements
  checklists, and analyze when useful or required. Existing full production gates
  remain in force; shorter work does not need ritual artifacts.
- Repair: installed bug extension, assess → fix → test → REA closeout before
  `verified`. Assessment and testing record evidence; only fix changes source.
  Failed tests return to diagnosis/fix.
- Idea assessment: installed assess extension, intake → research → define → shape
  → decide. A go verdict is not authorization to implement; a justified no-go can
  complete an assessment request.
- Existing code: specify the bounded requested change; do not retroactively
  specify or rewrite the whole application. Reuse its architecture and tests.

The local numbered-feature continuation is a user convention, not a Spec Kit
requirement. For remaining Final Goal slices, use the next feature without asking.
Within each feature preserve the project's living, flow-back, or flow-forward
artifact rules. Reconcile accepted changes at their owning artifact; never lower
requirements just to match an implementation defect.

## Native workflows and trust

Reuse an installed workflow's status/resume state if one owns this run. The native
engine already supports loops, conditional steps, fan-out/fan-in, overlays, and
checkpointed runs; do not build another scheduler to reproduce it. Inspect its
resolved steps before choosing it. Its human gates are not silently bypassed by
forged verdict inputs. Runtime `requires` is not a sandbox.

Presets customize existing behavior; extensions add capabilities; bundles package
components. Catalog presence is not a security audit. No automatic installs,
remote shell execution, forced refresh, or global profile changes are implied by
SDD. Preserve local modifications during any separately authorized upgrade.

For cross-component work, link the authoritative contract and consumer version.
Do not edit a consumer copy to invent provider support. Local contract checks,
actual integration, merged code, and deployed readiness are distinct evidence.

## Source entry points

- [Core phases](https://github.github.com/spec-kit/reference/agentic-sdd.html)
- [Core CLI and environment](https://github.github.com/spec-kit/reference/core.html)
- [Artifacts](https://github.github.com/spec-kit/reference/artifacts.html)
- [Workflows](https://github.github.com/spec-kit/reference/workflows.html)
- [Existing projects](https://github.github.com/spec-kit/guides/existing-projects.html)
- [Spec persistence](https://github.github.com/spec-kit/concepts/spec-persistence.html)
- [Monorepos](https://github.github.com/spec-kit/guides/monorepo.html)
- [Contracts](https://github.github.com/spec-kit/guides/contract-driven-development.html)
- [Bug fixing](https://github.github.com/spec-kit/guides/bugfix.html)
- [Assessment](https://github.github.com/spec-kit/guides/assessment.html)

The entrypoint stays short and references load conditionally, following the
[Agent Skills format](https://agentskills.io/specification) and
[authoring guidance](https://agentskills.io/skill-creation/best-practices).

<!-- file: references/phase-contract.md -->

# Phase contracts

Read the section for the phase being entered. Use the installed command's exact
contract when it differs; adapt the orchestration, not the command's authority.

Execution *inside* a phase (architect / arena / swarm / interrogate / poteto
non-negotiables) is defined in [pstack-integration.md](pstack-integration.md).
That file does not change artifact ownership below.

## Artifact ownership

- **Constitution:** preserve existing principles unless a change is authorized.
- **Specify:** record the requested behavior, non-goals, and observable acceptance;
  maintain the built-in requirements checklist as the installed command allows.
- **Clarify:** resolve non-authority ambiguities from repository evidence and
  recorded assumptions;
  record agent assumptions as assumptions, never as human answers. The built-in
  requirements checklist may be reevaluated here.
- **Plan:** reuse architecture and define the smallest approach and verification
  contract. Do not create test infrastructure unless directly necessary.
- **Checklist:** evaluate requirements quality, not implementation completion.
  Custom lists are reviewer-owned. An authorized reviewer may evaluate them;
  implementation does not edit their markers or silently approve them.
- **Tasks:** derive dependency-ordered work, exact ownership, and acceptance checks
  from the admitted plan. A prerequisite must trace to an existing acceptance gap.
- **Analyze:** read-only consistency analysis. Fix problems in their owning phase,
  then rerun analysis; do not modify source as part of this command.
- **Implement:** execute admitted tasks and focused checks. Read checklist state;
  route unresolved review to the authorized reviewer instead of ticking boxes.
- **Converge:** only after implementation of current tasks. Assess spec, plan, and
  tasks; append in-scope gaps to tasks.md and return to implement once. Converge
  runs one time per spec; remaining gaps after that round carry over to the next
  numbered spec. A clean converge leaves tasks unchanged. Do not edit code, delete tasks, or broaden requirements
  in the converge command. No reviewer score declares it converged.
- **REA closeout (after clean converge, not a Spec Kit command):** orchestration
  owned by `agentic-sdd`. Mandatory MCP/CLI Evidence pass before feature close
  or Final Goal finish. Install/setup only as [rea-closeout.md](rea-closeout.md)
  allows. Material findings get one bounded fix round and REA again; no
  second converge; further findings carry over to the next spec.

## Verification contract

In the existing plan/tasks/steering artifact record only what is useful:

`acceptance ID → check/repro → required observable result → code state → result`

Record command and outcome, relevant evidence path, and any unverified boundary.
Bind evidence to HEAD plus relevant dirty/untracked state, or a content identity
for Git-free work. Invalidate affected evidence after edits. A generated test,
command, or screenshot with no behavioral assertion is not execution proof.

Use repository-mandated checks plus the smallest proof of the changed behavior.
Do not attach E2E, profiles, heap snapshots, or independent reviewers to every edit.
Mocks prove the mock boundary only; they do not establish a real provider result.

Evidence classes: **static**, **test**, **runtime**, **provider**, **unverified**.
Required classes come from acceptance and repository policy, not a universal quota.
Missing obtainable evidence enters recovery. A genuinely unavailable dependency
blocks only affected acceptance; other admitted work continues. Neither a passing
score nor a retry budget converts missing evidence into success.

## Handoff

Record compactly in existing artifacts:

```text
PROJECT / SPEC ROOT / FEATURE / PHASE
CODE STATE: revision + dirty/untracked owners, or content identity
GOAL: requested outcome; remaining acceptance IDs
DONE / NEXT: artifacts, task IDs, next owning phase
CHECKS: commands, outcomes, evidence classes, current-state binding
RECOVERY: failure class, rejected hypothesis, next discriminating action
ROUTING: requested model/effort, observed run/model/effort or unknown
BUDGET: escalation passes consumed/remaining; host capability limits
BLOCKERS: precise dependency or authority boundary, if any
RESUME: pstack resume.mjs checkpoint path (Claude/Codex port) or none
```

With pstack present, write this block via the poteto `pause-safely` playbook
(`O-pause`) and read it back via `session-pickup`; `progress.md` stays
authoritative over the checkpoint. Receiving agents verify the snapshot before writing. Unexpected revision, feature,
or ownership changes require reconciliation, not resetting another writer's work.
Refresh after an authorized exact-path phase commit. Completion requires the
original outcome, current-state required checks, and REA disposition `pass` or
`not-applicable`, then stops further expansion.
