<!-- file: references/rea-closeout.md -->

---
description: Mandatory REA reverse-engineering closeout after Spec Kit converge / Final Goal finish. Includes install when missing.
---

# REA Closeout (Mandatory)

After a clean Spec Kit `converge` (or before writing bug `test` verdict
`verified`), and before declaring the feature or Final Goal finished, run a
**REA** analysis pass. Scores and chat review do not replace REA Evidence.

Do **not** treat REA as a Spec Kit phase command. Converge still only assesses
and appends tasks. Material REA findings get one bounded fix round: `implement` (features) or
`fix` (bugs) via recorded tasks/deviations, rerun the affected checks (no second
`converge`), then run REA again on the new code state. A further material
finding on the same spec carries over to the next small spec. Previous Evidence
IDs are stale after edits.

Installed `speckit-converge` reporting `converged` (review / PR / stop) is **not**
finish — run REA closeout on that code state first.

## When it is required

| Exit | REA required? |
|------|----------------|
| Feature `converge` clean (no new tasks) | **Yes** |
| Final Goal complete (no remaining admitted features) | **Yes** |
| Bug `test` before writing `verified` | **Yes** (scoped to the fix surface) |
| Light-path trivial-only exit | Same pass rule if a runnable/build artifact exists; else `not-applicable` with reason |
| Read-only audit / plan-only mode | Optional; **do not** install or mutate |

## Dispositions (finish rule)

| Disposition | Meaning | May finish Final Goal / feature / bug verified? |
|-------------|---------|--------------------------------------------------|
| `pass` | Real Evidence ID(s) present; required capture families for the artifact type; bound to current code state; no material findings | **Yes** |
| `not-applicable` | No runnable or build artifact exists (with recorded reason) | **Yes** |
| `tasks-appended` | Material findings queued for implement/fix | **No** — continue Spec Kit loop |
| `blocked-limitation` | Tooling failed after install/alternate path; command + exit + remediation recorded | **No** — stays open. A user dropping REA is a recorded scope change to `not-applicable` only when no runnable/build artifact exists, not a finish on this disposition |

**Material finding** means: acceptance miss, broken P1 path, page/runtime error
that violates acceptance, integrity contradiction, or user-visible wrong behavior.

`pass` requires at least one evidence id copied **verbatim** from the tool result
(not the placeholder string `ev_…`).

## Ensure REA is available

Prefer the host MCP server (`user-rea` / `rea` tools) when already connected.
Otherwise install the CLI, then wire **only the active host**.

### Detect

```sh
command -v rea >/dev/null && rea --version
# or: MCP exposes capture_browser_scenario / inspect_web_page / analyze_javascript_application
```

### Install CLI (delivery/repair closeout only)

Authorized **without** extra user quiz **only when**:

- Mode is delivery or repair closeout (not read-only / plan / audit), **and**
- MCP tools and `rea` CLI are both missing, **or** CLI exists but this host’s
  MCP registration is missing/stale for the active client id

```sh
# Node 22.19+ / 24.11+ / 26+ required. Abort if outside that set.
node -p "process.versions.node"
# Pin a known good package; do not upgrade a working CLI
npm install -g rea-agents@6.7.0
rea --version
```

Do **not** use `curl | bash` for this skill. Do **not** use `--all-detected`.

Optional engines reported unhealthy by `rea doctor` (Ghidra, IDA, jadx, Swift
helper) are **not** blockers when an alternate REA path for this artifact works.

### Wire agent MCP (active host only)

| Host | `rea setup --client` value |
|------|----------------------------|
| Claude Code | `claude_code` |
| Codex | `codex` |
| Cursor | `cursor` |
| Grok Build | `grok_build` |

`--client claude` and `--client grok` are **invalid** (VALIDATION_ERROR).

```sh
rea setup --dry-run --yes --client <active-id> --format json
rea setup --yes --client <active-id>
```

If MCP was just registered, reload/reconnect the agent MCP session before
continuing. If tools remain invisible, fall back to CLI
`rea capture-browser-scenario` / `rea analyze-javascript-application` / etc.

## What to run

Pick the **smallest** REA path that covers the delivered artifact:

| Deliverable | Preferred REA operations |
|-------------|--------------------------|
| Web / SPA | See **Web / SPA** below |
| Node / Electron JS app | MCP `analyze_javascript_application` or CLI `rea analyze-javascript-application` on build output (`detail: summary`); UI scenario if present |
| Native / mobile package | `analyze` / package inspect appropriate to the format |
| Pure library (tests only) | Static REA on built artifact + record test Evidence; no fake UI scenario |

Always:

1. Bind analysis to **current** code state (HEAD + relevant dirty paths, or content identity).
2. Record verbatim Evidence IDs in `progress.md` and `converge.md` (or bug `test.md`).
3. After the one implement/fix round from REA findings: invalidate prior REA IDs; rerun affected checks (no second converge); run REA again. Still material → `closed-carryover` into the next spec.

### Web / SPA

1. Serve the existing preview/build URL (do not invent a second app).
2. Run MCP `capture_browser_scenario` or CLI `rea capture-browser-scenario`.
   - **Launch** mode: provide a local browser `executable_path`.
   - **Connect** mode: only if a loopback CDP endpoint is **already** up; then
     `list_browser_targets` → use that `target_id`. A Vite URL is **not** a CDP endpoint.
3. `actions` must include the P1 control (`click` / `fill` / `press`), not only a wait.
4. Set capture **explicitly**. Required `at_end`: `url` **plus** `accessibility` or `dom`;
   add `storage` when acceptance touches storage. Required `events`: `console`,
   `page-errors`, `network`.
5. A URL-only default capture is **not** a pass.
6. `inspect_web_page` / `rea inspect-web-page` is an optional passive follow-up.
   It cannot navigate or click and **cannot** alone satisfy P1.

### Failure handling

| Failure | Action |
|---------|--------|
| REA not installed | Install per above (closeout scope), retry once |
| MCP not visible after setup | Reconnect MCP; else CLI equivalents |
| Provider toolchain broken | Try alternate REA path (scenario vs static). If all fail → `blocked-limitation` (does **not** finish) |
| Material defect | One bounded fix round, affected checks, then REA again; still material → carry over to next spec |
| Flaky observation | One discriminating retry; then unresolved / tasks |
| `cleanup_incomplete` with `live candidates <pid>=environment_unavailable`, even on `/usr/bin/true`; intermittent | rea-agents ≤ 6.6 fails closed when an unrelated same-user process whose environment is withheld (`CS_RESTRICT` images such as Chrome Helper renderers) starts during the capture. Verified on macOS 26: 6.4.0 fails, 6.7.0 records those PIDs as `restricted_process_environment_withheld` and passes. Pin `rea-agents@6.7.0` or newer in the host MCP config (`~/.claude.json`, `~/.cursor/mcp.json`, `~/.codex/config.toml`, `~/.grok/config.toml`) and restart that server. Until then, retry through the CLI (`npx -y rea-agents@6.7.0 capture-process scenario.json --format json --full-output`, scenario keys `executable`, `arguments`, `working_directory`, `environment`, `timeout_ms`, `finalization_ms`) and record its Evidence. Reconnecting an old-version server does not fix it |
| `capture_process_failed` with `xcrun`/`swiftc` `redefinition of module 'SwiftBridging'` | Command Line Tools older than macOS (e.g. CLT 16.4 on macOS 26): `sudo softwareupdate -i "Command Line Tools for Xcode <os version>"` from a real terminal (sudo needs a TTY); verify with `xcrun swiftc` on the package's `bridge/process/*.swift` |
| Source-only interpreted script (no binary/bundle) | `open_binary` is n/a; use `capture_process_scenario` on the real command. If the host capture helper itself fails (toolchain error), that is `blocked-limitation` with the host fix named in `Next action`, not `not-applicable` |

Never mark Final Goal complete with a silent skipped REA when a runnable
artifact exists and REA could be installed under the rules above.

## Progress / converge recording template

```markdown
## REA closeout
- Tooling: MCP user-rea | CLI rea@x.y.z | installed-this-session: yes/no
- Host setup client: cursor | claude_code | codex | grok_build
- Artifact: <path or URL + revision/dirty binding>
- Evidence IDs: <paste verbatim ids from tool output>
- Findings: none | <short list>
- Disposition: pass | not-applicable | tasks-appended | blocked-limitation
- If blocked-limitation: command, exit, alternate tried, remediation
```

## Hard rules

- REA closeout is mandatory for Spec Kit delivery/repair exits in the table above.
- Install/setup authorization is **narrow**: delivery/repair closeout only; active
  host client id only; pinned package when installing; no remote-shell installer.
- Installing Spec Kit extensions/presets/integrations still requires confirmation.
- Do not weaken Spec Kit acceptance to satisfy REA; fix or task-track instead.

---

<!-- file: references/recovery.md -->

# Collaborative recovery without scope drift

Use for repeated failure, conflicting evidence, or verification that is starting
to expand the product. A retry threshold triggers a change of method, not an
arbitrary end to the user's goal. Clear small failures can be fixed directly.

## Detect verification loops by evidence, not elapsed time alone

Before a verification batch, name the acceptance condition it can establish and
what result would change the next action. Use existing commands and checkpoints.
If it establishes neither a required condition nor resolves a specific uncertainty,
skip that optional check and do the next admitted delivery task.

Reuse a passing result when its relevant implementation, inputs, environment,
test/oracle, and required freshness have not changed. A documentation-only edit
does not by itself invalidate UI evidence. Shared dependency/token/schema changes
can invalidate many consumers; do not pretend those are isolated. Run narrow
checks during repair, then the required integration/full matrix at its declared
checkpoint once the relevant batch stabilizes. Repository-mandated cadence wins.

**Progress** means new valid acceptance evidence, a concrete in-scope defect found,
a defect repaired, or an observation that eliminates a live hypothesis. A new
screenshot filename, larger report, repeated green run, reviewer agreement, model
switch, or higher reviewer confidence alone is not progress. Slow work that is reducing
real gaps is not a verification loop.

After two attempts of the same check with no such progress, or an earlier sign
of scope drift, enter the checkpoint below instead of another same-state run.
With pstack present, two failed fixes sharing one premise trigger
`principle-attack-the-premise`: write the premise down and test it directly
before another fix; use `why` for regression history.
Count each check separately: progress in another check cannot clear its loop,
and one stuck check cannot block an independent check that has not run yet.
After a real implementation/input/environment/oracle change, allow the first
observation on that basis; if the same failure persists, its loop history remains.
An attempt can include a batch of checks; do not instrument every tool call. Carry
this history across reviewer/model changes and compaction. Record only:

`acceptance → last outcome → evidence/diagnosis delta → chosen next action`

Count attempts from the record with code, not by estimate. This
threshold changes the method, not the required checks or the overall goal.

## Bound the whole feature, not only one check

`converge` runs once per spec. After its single bounded fix round, reconcile
a complete remaining-gap list in the existing tasks/steering artifact and move
it into the next, smaller numbered spec (`closed-carryover`) instead of another
converge: `acceptance ID → concrete defect/missing evidence → owner → smallest
repair/observation → affected checks`. Group duplicate findings. Keep required
failures open; move unrelated discoveries to separately admitted future work.
A changing score without new evidence is not a new gap. Keep closed bundles closed
unless a concrete defect or relevant source change invalidates their evidence.
Report open blocking defects and missing required evidence, not task percentage.

Before an expensive full matrix, state which relevant inputs changed and why
those changes invalidate the full scope. Prefer per-case evidence reuse when
only a story or review classification changed. Shared tokens, dependencies,
fixtures, oracle behavior or a declared final integration checkpoint can justify
a full run. `run_check` permits execution; it does not choose the cheapest scope.
Preserve failed commands. A missing manual-review row may be resolved by a separate
review of its preserved raw evidence without pretending the failed command passed.

Use a stable logical check ID and recipe across attempts. Output folder names and
new timestamps are not new acceptance checkpoints. Keep generated evidence out
of source basis; use the runner's snapshots for run-specific artifacts. If a
recipe truly changes, retain its history and inspect the affected evidence.

Keep one current checkpoint in the existing feature steering artifact. Other
handoff/roadmap documents link to it instead of duplicating live counts. Date and
label historical receipts so compaction cannot promote them to current state.

## Evidence-backed guard and execution

Use `scripts/verification_guard.py --state progress.json --evidence-root PROJECT`
for read-only judgment before an expensive/repeated check. Use the collector in
[verification execution](verification-execution.md) for actual approved commands.
It records process results and source/log/artifact hashes and enforces the guard
before execution. Do not fabricate a pass entry or its hashes to reuse evidence.

A missing/changed receipt, log, declared artifact, source, command, or declared
environment invalidates reuse. `required_gaps` stays open. `repair_state` means
repair current metadata/recipe, not run the same test again. `run_check` permits
the admitted check; `recover` requires a different action; `reuse_pass` avoids
only a redundant check. None declares the full product complete.

Keep old records even when their checkpoint or evidence is unavailable. An
unscoped historical `always` pass never satisfies the current checkpoint; it
appears in `legacy_unscoped_history` and a fresh current run may proceed. Missing
metadata for an unselected optional check does not block unrelated required work.
Never guess historical IDs or discard failures. Only a selected `always` check
with no CURRENT checkpoint needs `repair_state` before it can run.

Per-check counters prevent one stuck check from blocking fresh independent work,
or another check's success from hiding its loop. A real basis change permits its
first check; an unchanged repeated failure remains a recovery signal. For an
`always` check, a verified pass within the current checkpoint can be reused;
a new actual CI/release/batch checkpoint requires fresh evidence.

A new adapter/monitor is allowed when an existing path cannot obtain required
proof or retain progress state. Record its necessity, bounded ownership, and
acceptance. Extend an existing runner first; framework work is a prerequisite
of the original goal, never a new implicit product goal.

## Progress checkpoint: choose once, perform one action

Write down the original goal, remaining acceptance, the last two attempts and their
computed per-check/aggregate counts, validity of existing evidence, current failure, and
an enumerated set of actions. Decide `verification_loop` and `next_move` from
those facts in one pass; pick model/effort for the chosen action at the same time.

Choose only an action supported by the current facts:

- **resume_delivery:** reuse sufficient valid evidence and implement the next
  admitted task; finish only if the original goal and all required gates are met.
- **targeted_check:** make one observation that separates named hypotheses or
  supplies a missing required result; name the predicted difference first.
- **repair_product:** fix a reproduced defect in the owning implementation phase,
  then rerun the affected acceptance check.
- **repair_harness:** use an existing supported tool/environment path or correct a
  demonstrated oracle defect without changing the intended product condition.
  Harness work must be a necessary, bounded prerequisite, not a new platform.
- **external_block:** record a concrete unavailable dependency/authority boundary
  after relevant alternatives were checked; continue other admitted work.

A high loop score rejects the redundant proposed check; it does not waive a failed
required gate. The primary decides from these facts and rules. Do not summon more
reviewers or change models without new evidence. One independent challenger can help resolve a real conflict;
otherwise make the smallest discriminating observation and proceed.

Execute the chosen action before the next judgment. If it fails with no delta,
exclude that unchanged approach and choose a materially different hypothesis or
available path. Do not reset the counter by renaming a check. Stop only the
nonproductive verification branch, not the original delivery objective. Never
change an assertion merely to make a failure disappear.

## Diagnose before adding work

Classify with evidence, keeping uncertainty explicit:

- **Change defect:** reproduce the failure in the changed path; fix in implement.
- **Existing defect:** compare against a safe baseline when useful. Repair only if
  it is a necessary prerequisite for original acceptance; otherwise report it
  separately. Do not waive a required gate just because it previously failed.
- **Environment/tool gap:** repair the owned local setup or use an equivalent
  supported observation path. Do not alter product behavior for tool convenience.
- **Requirement/test conflict:** distinguish an incorrect test from a real defect.
  Reconcile the owning artifact without weakening the original outcome.
- **Authority/external block:** identify the missing authorization, ownership, or
  dependency. Do not make it disappear with a score or majority vote.

A prerequisite is admitted only when it names the original acceptance ID, shows
why that condition cannot pass without it, and is the smallest compatible repair
within authorized scope. Record its task and evidence. A broad refactor, new
framework, or new product behavior is not automatically a prerequisite.

## Deliberate briefly, then act

1. The primary pins goal, current code state, failed check, and the next uncertainty.
   Give one independent reviewer the raw relevant evidence and bounded question.
   Request their diagnosis before showing the primary's preferred explanation.
2. Compare hypotheses and at most a few concrete alternatives. Collaborators
   advise; the primary retains the decision. Use another specialist only if an
   unresolved consequential disagreement warrants it. No standing committee.
3. Make the direction/model/effort choice once from the enumerated options.
   Arithmetic and permission decisions are never delegated to a reviewer.
   Record the reason the evidence supports the chosen action.
4. If diagnoses disagree, run the smallest reversible observation that distinguishes
   them. Consensus means an actionable hypothesis supported by evidence, not
   unanimity or repeated voting. Do not wait for every agent to agree.
5. Apply one scoped action in its owning phase, then rerun the original affected
   check. Continue until acceptance is met. If a test was wrong, document the
   contradiction and use a corrected check of the same intended behavior.

One writer per checkout. Reviewers do not concurrently fix the worker's files.
With limited slots, serialize review. If delegation fails or is unavailable,
perform an explicit counter-hypothesis review in the primary and disclose that
independent consensus was unavailable; continue useful authorized work.

## Prevent both drift and abandonment

Track only `failure → hypothesis → action → observation → next` in the existing
artifact. A repeated action with the same result and no new evidence changes
hypothesis, tool path, or assignee. Increasing effort is appropriate for reasoning
difficulty, not missing credentials, unsupported tools, or a broken environment.
Once uncertainty resolves, return to the lowest capable model/effort.

A local retry cap cannot end the overall task. Explicit user/runtime budgets still
apply: preserve a resumable handoff if those prevent further work. An affected path
can be blocked only by a concrete unsatisfied dependency/authority boundary after
relevant available alternatives were checked. Continue independent admitted tasks;
when no useful work remains, report the exact needed input and remaining acceptance.
Do not poll, invent tasks, bypass required gates, or claim completion to avoid a stop.

When original acceptance and required checks pass, stop expanding verification.
Resume a passing check only after new changes, failures, or a concrete unresolved
risk justify it. No new validation platform is required by this recovery procedure.

---

<!-- file: references/direction-keeper.md -->

# Direction keeping

Read when steering a phase, recovering, or advancing to the next feature. Pin the
Final Goal in existing `steering.md` or the project's equivalent artifact. Keep
admitted acceptance and non-goals stable; implementation discovery may change the
method or reveal a necessary prerequisite, not authorize a new product outcome.

## Phase and recovery gate

At each meaningful phase transition or recovery decision, enumerate concrete next
moves and pick child model/effort as described in model-routing.md. Judge each
move against goal, current artifacts/evidence, and constraints on these heads:

- `next_move`: continue, repair, investigate, reconcile_artifacts, or external_block.
- `in_scope`: the next action serves an admitted acceptance condition.
- `invented`: the proposal introduces unrelated behavior or verification machinery.
- `authority_conflict`: the proposal violates an unresolved authority boundary.
- `recoverable`: missing evidence can be obtained within available authority/tools.
- At a no-progress checkpoint, `verification_loop`: the proposed check repeats
  valid evidence or unchanged failure without resolving a named uncertainty.
  Use the recovery reference's concrete actions for `next_move`: resume_delivery,
  targeted_check, repair_product, repair_harness, external_block.

Compute counts and costs with code first. No reviewer grants authorization or
attests unrun tests. When a real fork remains after the written rules, use one
independent pstack reviewer (`interrogate` / `arena`); otherwise primary judgment,
recorded, and continue.

A blocking authority/out-of-scope check at probability >= 0.7 overrides a continue
label. Reject that action and choose an in-scope path; it does not automatically
stop unrelated admitted work. Missing obtainable evidence routes to recovery.
At the recovery no-progress checkpoint, include the original goal, remaining
acceptance, recent attempt outcomes, evidence validity, and the compact
`verification_guard.py` result in state. Its count is computed from the complete
checkpoint history. Use the declared evidence root so file/source integrity is
checked before reuse; a legacy self-report cannot establish a pass. Use
the selected-check counter to diagnose its loop, without masking it with another
check's progress or blocking fresh independent checks. For `always` checks, only
the actual current checkpoint's result satisfies its cadence. A loop finding at probability >= 0.7 rejects the
redundant check, not its underlying requirement. Execute one selected action
before asking again. Do not re-score unchanged evidence or invalidate passing
checks merely because another agent wants its own receipt.
For `review`/`abstain`/`uncertain`, inspect the evidence and act under the written
rule. Low confidence is not a reason to keep re-judging: use the least disruptive
admissible action or a discriminating check.

Record the chosen action and reason, actual check outcome,
and requested/observed routing. Then execute; do not substitute a receipt for
work. Invoke the recovery reference when a real disagreement needs collaborators.

## Acceptance coverage before advancing

Converge runs once per spec. Gaps that survive its single fix round become the
next numbered spec's scope (`closed-carryover`); do not reopen converge on the
current spec.

After installed `converge` reports converged, run REA closeout before the next
feature or finish ([rea-closeout.md](rea-closeout.md)). Continue admitted Final
Goal work when any acceptance or REA disposition is still open (`tasks-appended`
or `blocked-limitation` are not finish).

After installed `converge` reports converged, reconcile the full spec's acceptance
conditions with the check inventory. `criterion_gate.py` extracts English listed
Given/When/Then scenarios, not every prose requirement, success metric, or language.
For other formats or additional criteria, provide the COMPLETE reviewed list as
`[{"id":"AC-1","text":"..."}, ...]` using `--criteria-file`. Do not silently
narrow coverage to what a regex recognizes or replace the canonical spec.

```sh
python scripts/criterion_gate.py questions --spec path/to/spec.md
# For more than 64 criteria, use --batch 1, --batch 2, ...; preserve all IDs.
python scripts/criterion_gate.py decide --spec path/to/spec.md \
  --answers-file criterion-answers.json
```

`--criteria-file` replaces `--spec` in either command. Enumerate the complete
reviewed list, including prose requirements, before execution. An independent
reviewer may examine changed or uncertain criteria in bounded evidence packets; completeness is checked
against the full list, not by repeatedly rescoring every passing criterion.

`decide` now requires `--review-file review.json --evidence-root PROJECT` before
it can return `advance=true`. Scores-only callers receive `advance=false` with
`evidence_review_required`; old score files remain historical advisory data.
`--answers-file` is optional; the primary's own adjudication may be used. A low score asks the primary
to inspect a named uncertainty; it is not a reproduced defect or a new task.
Resolve it once against the source and actual check evidence. Record the concrete
reason; retain unmet/blocked for real gaps. Respect reviewer-owned decisions.

The review is a compact index in the existing feature evidence directory:

```json
{
  "criteria_digest": "digest returned by a scores-only decide call",
  "reviewer": "authorized primary or reviewer identity",
  "decisions": [{
    "id": "AC-1",
    "status": "met",
    "reason": "Current reload test observed the same saved value.",
    "basis": [{"path": "src/store.py", "sha256": "actual 64-character hash"}],
    "evidence": [{"path": "proofs/save.json", "sha256": "actual 64-character hash"}]
  }]
}
```

Every criterion appears exactly once. Status is `met`, `unmet`, or `blocked`.
For `met`, include the relevant implementation, input, dependency/environment
manifest and oracle files in `basis`, plus actual receipts/results in `evidence`.
Use root-relative paths and real hashes. The helper validates complete coverage,
criteria identity, path confinement and current content hashes; it does not prove
that an assertion is meaningful or a reviewer's claim is true. The authorized
reviewer must read the evidence. Never fabricate an adjudication to defeat a gate.
Unknown/missing/duplicate IDs and stale references fail closed.

Reuse a previously reviewed criterion while its acceptance and relevant basis
remain valid. New evidence for another criterion does not reopen it. A changed
criterion list requires reconciliation with the new digest, not automatic reruns
of unaffected behavior. Explicitly record the concrete defect or affected basis
that reopens a met item. Numeric confidence alone is insufficient.

Exit codes: 0 reviewed coverage passes, 1 review/gaps remain, 2 invalid input or
stale evidence. `completion_decided=false` always: required checks, actual
convergence, reviewer authority, and merge/release gates remain separate. A review
index is not a security attestation and never replaces raw execution receipts.
If REA is `pass` or `not-applicable` and no admitted Final Goal work remains,
finish. If work remains, specify the next feature. Never finish on
`blocked-limitation` or `tasks-appended`.

## Clarification and checklist authority

Resolve ordinary implementation ambiguity with evidence and recorded assumptions,
not pretend human answers. Repair requirements gaps in specify/clarify, design
gaps in plan, and task gaps in tasks. Analyze stays read-only; converge stays
append-only. Custom checklist reviews go to their authorized owner. An explicitly
human-owned decision cannot be forged by an agent or reviewer; complete all independent
work before requesting the specific missing input.

---

<!-- file: references/verification-execution.md -->

# Verification execution

Use for repeatable, already admitted CLI checks where collecting real evidence
or preventing a redundant run matters. Python 3.10+ and standard library only;
the current runner is exercised on POSIX. It is not a sandbox or authorization
service. Review the command against repository policy before `--execute`.

## Declare the existing check

Keep a small execution snapshot alongside existing feature artifacts. The spec
and plan remain authority. No new requirements are admitted by this JSON.

```json
{
  "goal_id": "feature-004",
  "checkpoint_id": "implementation-batch-1",
  "proposed_check": "save",
  "checks": [{
    "id": "save", "criteria": ["AC-1"], "required": true,
    "rerun_policy": "on_change",
    "command": ["python3", "-B", "checks/save.py"],
    "basis_sources": {
      "implementation": ["src/store.py"],
      "inputs": ["fixtures/input.json", "specs/004-save/spec.md"],
      "oracle": ["checks/save.py"]
    },
    "environment_keys": ["APP_ENV"],
    "environment_id": "local-test-instance",
    "observation_json_key": "observation",
    "artifacts": ["proofs/save.json"]
  }],
  "history": []
}
```

Paths are relative to an explicit owned project root. Declare all relevant source,
lockfile/dependency, fixture, and oracle files; do not include self-updating state
or generated outputs in basis_sources. Declare required proof outputs in artifacts.
Environment values are hashed, not copied into the receipt. The actual executable,
cwd, Python/platform, declared environment, and harness version are fingerprinted.
Undeclared dependencies cannot be verified automatically.

`observation_json_key` selects a stable top-level field from stdout JSON. Exclude
timestamps, filenames, and incidental counters. If absent, the runner uses the
conservative outcome/exit-code pair; a recovery review must inspect the logs to
distinguish different failures. Do not build a custom reporter if an existing
structured reporter already supplies suitable facts.

## Preview, execute once, inspect

```sh
python scripts/verification_run.py --state progress.json --root /owned/project
python scripts/verification_run.py --state progress.json --root /owned/project --execute
```

`--check ID` selects another admitted check. Loading a state file never executes
its command by itself. `--execute` runs the approved argv with shell=False only
when the guard returns run_check. It is not permission to run untrusted repository
commands, external/production actions, or prohibited browser drivers. For GUI
verification, use the allowed host tools and an appropriate evidence adapter.

The runner holds a state-writer lock, captures stdout/stderr and exit status,
checks fingerprints before and after, snapshots declared proof outputs per run,
then publishes a receipt and an atomic
history update. The state reference is the commit: orphan receipts from a conflict
are not automatically imported or treated as accepted evidence. Other writers'
state changes are preserved. Do not delete a lock until its actual owner/state
is understood. Interrupted runs can leave a lock or orphan; diagnose rather than
launching duplicate work or discarding history.

Timeout defaults to 60 seconds (`--timeout` can set a justified bound). Combined
output defaults to 1 MiB and is capped at 2 MiB. Only the process group started by
this run is killed on timeout/output overflow. A timeout, malformed observation,
missing declared proof, source change during execution, or state conflict cannot
produce an accepted pass. Proof artifacts are bounded to 64 MiB each; use a
reviewed compact extract/reference for larger profiling data.

Exit codes: 0 pass/reuse/read-only plan, 1 failed/error check, 2 invalid input,
3 recovery/state action required, 4 state/lock conflict. A subprocess exit 0
with contradictory same-basis evidence returns recovery rather than an accepted pass. Parse the JSON;
0 from a read-only plan is not execution success. A `run_check` decision is permission under the guard, not a requirement to run
the entire matrix; select the affected check scope first using recovery.md. Keep
logical check IDs and command recipes stable across output-only changes.
Commands are not retried by
this helper. The primary's recovery loop chooses the next action.

## Reuse and legacy records

A reusable receipt must match actual file/log/artifact SHA-256, goal, check,
checkpoint, command, current source/environment/harness basis, and successful
process flags. A made-up path or missing SHA never counts as a pass. The guard
recomputes basis from declared files even when a stored snapshot is stale.

Legacy rows are preserved. An old always row without checkpoint_id cannot satisfy
a current checkpoint, but it does not prohibit a fresh run or block another check.
Name the CURRENT checkpoint from the actual planned execution before an always
check; do not invent old IDs. The collector appends a new verifiable record.

Checks still need meaningful assertions and an honest declared dependency scope.
Hash integrity detects missing/stale/changed material; it does not defend against
an actor who can rewrite the validator, oracle, state, and every hash together.
Production trust may require a separately controlled CI verifier. Do not label
this local helper as that security boundary or equate an empty required_gaps list with the
original product's acceptance/convergence.

---

<!-- file: references/host-guide-greenfield-brownfield.md -->

---
description: >
  Dual-audience (human + agent) guide for running agentic-sdd with pstack on
  Claude Code, Codex, and Cursor. Split into greenfield (new Spec Kit project)
  and brownfield (existing codebase / existing Spec Kit). Process authority
  stays Spec Kit; pstack is execution style inside phases.
---

# Host guide: greenfield & brownfield (Claude · Codex · Cursor)

**Readers:** humans setting up or supervising a run; agents executing
`/agentic-sdd` (or `$agentic-sdd`). Agents treat this as procedure, not
permission to expand scope or install tools beyond what `SKILL.md` already
authorizes.

**Related (do not duplicate here):**

| File | Role |
|------|------|
| [`SKILL.md`](../SKILL.md) | Entrypoint, autonomy, hard boundaries |
| [`pstack-integration.md`](pstack-integration.md) | Phase → pstack obligation map |
| [`phase-contract.md`](phase-contract.md) | What each Spec Kit phase may write |
| [`cursor-continuation.md`](cursor-continuation.md) | Cursor `sdd-continue` stop-hook |
| [`rea-closeout.md`](rea-closeout.md) | Mandatory post-converge REA |
| `setup-speckit-multi-agent` skill | Init / inspect / activate / multi-host setup |

---

## 1. Mental model (both field types)

```text
Final Goal          ← what the human asked for (unchanged until delivered)
agentic-sdd         ← owns phase order, continuity, recovery, REA
Spec Kit            ← owns artifacts (.specify/, specs|/.specify/specs/, constitution)
pstack              ← owns how a batch is designed/reviewed/verified inside a phase
Host (Claude/Codex/Cursor) ← invocation surface only; never a second spec tree
```

| Layer | Greenfield | Brownfield |
|-------|------------|------------|
| Spec Kit | Create `.specify/` + first feature | Reuse or add Spec Kit **without** rewriting the whole app |
| First feature | Product slice from Final Goal | **Bounded change** only (one capability / bug / seam) |
| Architecture | Invented in `plan`, constrained by constitution | **Reuse** existing layout, tests, patterns |
| pstack | Full map from day one | Prefer `/how` + `/why` before `/architect`; smaller diffs |
| Risk | Wrong shape early | Blast radius + regressions |

**Invariant:** one checkout = one writer. One canonical spec root
(`specs/` or legacy `.specify/specs/`). Never fork specs per agent.

---

## 2. One-time machine setup (humans)

Do this once per machine. Agents do **not** auto-install pstack as part of SDD
(unless the user explicitly asked to set up pstack).

### 2.1 agentic-sdd (all hosts)

Canonical path (already symlinked on this machine):

```text
~/.agents/skills/agentic-sdd/
  → ~/.claude/skills/agentic-sdd
  → ~/.codex/skills/agentic-sdd
  → ~/.cursor/skills/agentic-sdd
```

### 2.2 pstack by host

| Host | Install (prefer user / global scope) | Invoke |
|------|--------------------------------------|--------|
| **Cursor** | `/add-plugin pstack` or marketplace install | `/poteto-mode`, `/architect`, `/arena`, … |
| **Claude Code** | `claude plugin install pstack --marketplace michael-denyer/pstack-claude --scope user` | `/pstack:architect`, `/pstack:interrogate`, … |
| **Codex** | Same marketplace/port via Codex plugin commands (see port README) | `pstack:…` / `$…` per port docs |

Then once per host: Cursor `/setup-pstack`; Claude `/pstack:setup-pstack`.

### 2.3 Spec Kit CLI + multi-agent helper

- `specify` CLI available on PATH.
- For multi-host projects: `setup-speckit-multi-agent` (`scripts/speckit_multi_agent.py setup|inspect|activate|sdd`).

### 2.4 Verify before first real run

```bash
# Claude global pstack
claude plugin list | grep pstack
# expect pstack@pstack-claude (user)

# Spec Kit
specify --version
test -d ~/.agents/skills/agentic-sdd && echo agentic-sdd ok
```

---

## 3. GREENFIELD — new product / empty repo

**Definition:** no meaningful application code yet, or a brand-new directory.
You are allowed to choose stack and layout subject to constitution + Final Goal.

### 3.1 Human checklist (greenfield)

1. Create an empty directory (prefer `~/Projects/<name>`).
2. Init Spec Kit (pick the host you will primarily use, then add others):

```bash
cd ~/Projects
specify init my-app --non-interactive --integration claude
# add peers as needed:
cd my-app
specify integration install cursor-agent
specify integration install codex   # if available in your Spec Kit build
# multi-agent helper (optional but recommended):
# setup-speckit-multi-agent setup --project "$PWD" --default claude
```

3. Confirm `.specify/`, constitution template, and integration status:

```bash
specify integration status --json
```

4. Open the project in the chosen host and start:

| Host | What to type |
|------|----------------|
| Cursor | `/agentic-sdd` then Final Goal + “greenfield; full Spec Kit” |
| Claude | `/agentic-sdd` (or attach skill) + same Final Goal |
| Codex | `$agentic-sdd` + Final Goal |

5. Optional: `/setup-pstack` or `/pstack:setup-pstack` if not done machine-wide.
6. Walk away. Approve shell/MCP cards only. Expect `progress.md` updates.
7. Finish criteria: feature REA `pass` or `not-applicable`, Final Goal closed or next numbered feature started without a quiz.

### 3.2 Agent procedure (greenfield)

Mode: **delivery**. Full-autonomy grant inside Final Goal.

```text
1. Confirm greenfield: little/no app code; .specify/ present or setup skill required.
2. If .specify/ missing → stop mutating; tell human to run setup-speckit-multi-agent
   / specify init (do not invent a second process).
3. Pin Final Goal + first acceptance slice in feature artifacts.
4. Run Spec Kit in order (no phase quiz):
   constitution (if empty) → specify → [clarify] → plan → [checklist] → tasks
   → implement → [analyze] → converge → REA → next feature while Goal remains
5. Inside each phase, apply pstack map (pstack-integration.md):
   - plan: O-architect / O-arena
   - implement: O-poteto (+ O-swarm / O-arena when warranted)
   - converge: O-interrogate + multi-perspective-review
6. Flush progress.md every meaningful stage.
   Cursor: maintain <!-- sdd-continue: ... --> (cursor-continuation.md).
7. Do not ask “should I go to plan?” — advance automatically.
8. Hard stop only for destructive / secrets / scope / missing Spec Kit project.
```

### 3.3 Greenfield phase expectations

| Phase | Produce | pstack emphasis | Do not |
|-------|---------|-----------------|--------|
| constitution | Project principles | unslop on prose | Invent unrelated product scope |
| specify | Observable AC, non-goals | sharpen / in-your-own-words if fuzzy | Skip AC |
| plan | Smallest stack + verification contract | architect; arena if 2+ shapes | Over-scaffold frameworks |
| tasks | Ordered Txxx with checks | sequence-verifiable-units | Tasks without AC links |
| implement | Code meeting AC | poteto non-negotiables; prove-it-works | Free-standing poteto playbook replacing Spec Kit |
| converge | Gap list or clean | interrogate | Relax AC to go green |
| REA | Disposition recorded | (not pstack) | Mark finished without REA |

### 3.4 Greenfield prompts (copy/paste)

**Cursor / Claude:**

```text
/agentic-sdd
Final Goal: <one sentence product outcome>
Field: greenfield
Hosts available: Claude + Cursor (shared .specify/)
Constraints: <stack prefs if any; else choose and record>
Done when: <observable AC> + REA pass/not-applicable
Run unattended through Spec Kit phases. No phase quiz.
```

**Codex:**

```text
$agentic-sdd
Final Goal: ...
Field: greenfield
...
```

### 3.5 Greenfield anti-patterns

- Starting `/pstack:poteto-mode` as the **only** process (skips Spec Kit artifacts).
- Generating a huge monorepo before one verified vertical slice.
- Asking the human which phase is next.
- Creating agent-specific `specs-claude/` trees.

---

## 4. BROWNFIELD — existing codebase

**Definition:** real application code, tests, or deployables exist. Spec Kit may
be absent, partial, or already active. Default stance: **smallest change that
meets the Final Goal**; do not retro-specify the entire system.

### 4.1 Classify the brownfield case

| Case | Signal | First move |
|------|--------|------------|
| **B1** Spec Kit already active | `.specify/` + feature pointer | `inspect` / `sdd` → continue owning phase |
| **B2** Code yes, Spec Kit no | App exists; no `.specify/` | Human-authorized `specify init --here` / `setup --init-existing` on **clean** baseline |
| **B3** Spec Kit stale / wrong feature | Pointer ≠ branch or tasks empty vs dirty tree | Reconcile pointer before edits |
| **B4** Bug / regression | Broken existing behavior | Bug workflow if installed; else bounded feature |
| **B5** Cross-cutting refactor | Large blast radius | `figure-it-out` + show-me-your-work; still Spec Kit features |

Agents: for **B2**, do **not** run `--init-existing` / `--force` without explicit
user authorization. Point to `setup-speckit-multi-agent`.

### 4.2 Human checklist (brownfield)

#### B1 — Spec Kit already present

```bash
cd /path/to/repo
# optional multi-agent health:
# setup-speckit-multi-agent inspect --project "$PWD" --full
specify integration status --json
# activate the host you will write with:
# setup-speckit-multi-agent activate claude|cursor|codex --project "$PWD"
```

Then in that host:

```text
/agentic-sdd
Final Goal: <bounded outcome>
Field: brownfield
Continue active feature if aligned; else specify next numbered feature for this Goal.
Do not rewrite unrelated subsystems.
```

#### B2 — Add Spec Kit to an existing repo

1. Clean Git working tree (or explicitly accept dirty ownership).
2. Review what `specify init --here` / multi-agent `--init-existing` will write.
3. Authorize setup once:

```bash
# Example — prefer the project's established helper:
# setup-speckit-multi-agent setup --project "$PWD" --default cursor --init-existing
# Or:
specify init --here --force --non-interactive --integration cursor-agent
specify integration install claude
```

4. Commit the Spec Kit scaffolding as its own commit when policy allows.
5. Start `/agentic-sdd` with a **narrow** first feature (one seam), not “spec the app”.

#### B3 — Reconcile before coding

- Align `.specify/feature.json` (or equivalent) with the feature directory and
  branch policy.
- List dirty paths; one writer owns them.
- Only then continue implement / specify.

### 4.3 Agent procedure (brownfield)

```text
1. Resolve nearest .specify/; record revision + dirty owners.
2. Classify B1–B5. If B2 without authorization → blocked/missing setup, ask once.
3. Pin Final Goal; derive a BOUNDARY: admitted paths, non-goals, required checks
   from repo policy + existing tests.
4. Orient with evidence before design:
   - pstack O-sharpen if Goal text is fuzzy
   - Cursor /how|/why or Claude /pstack:how|/pstack:why on the touched subsystem
5. specify only the requested change (spec-kit-alignment: existing code).
6. plan must reuse architecture; call O-architect only when crossing a new boundary.
7. tasks: small verifiable units; prefer repo test commands already present.
8. implement: poteto non-negotiables; O-blast before risky merges; O-tdd when cheap.
9. converge + O-interrogate; never lower AC to match a defect.
10. REA closeout; then next numbered feature only for remaining Goal work.
```

### 4.4 Brownfield phase expectations

| Phase | Brownfield bias | pstack emphasis |
|-------|-----------------|-----------------|
| specify | Bound the change; link existing behaviors as context, not full rewrite | how / why first |
| plan | Reuse modules, test harness, CI | architect only if new seam; arena if two migrations compete |
| tasks | Map to existing packages/packages owners | sequence-verifiable-units |
| implement | Minimal diff; migrate callers then delete | poteto; blast-radius; correct on repeated mistakes |
| converge | Regressions + AC | interrogate; multi-perspective |
| bug path | assess → fix → test | tdd when local oracle exists |

### 4.5 Brownfield prompts (copy/paste)

**Continue existing Spec Kit feature:**

```text
/agentic-sdd
Final Goal: <same Goal as progress.md if present>
Field: brownfield (B1)
Read progress.md + active feature; continue owning phase.
No phase quiz. Preserve dirty ownership. Shared specs only.
```

**New bounded feature on existing app:**

```text
/agentic-sdd
Final Goal: <bounded user-visible outcome>
Field: brownfield
Admitted paths: <dirs/packages>
Non-goals: <do not refactor X>
Required checks: <existing test/lint commands>
Start specify for the next numbered feature. Reuse architecture.
```

**Bug:**

```text
/agentic-sdd
Mode: repair
Field: brownfield
Symptom: <repro>
Use Spec Kit bug workflow if installed; else bounded fix feature.
Verify with the failing case before and after.
```

### 4.6 Brownfield anti-patterns

- “While we’re here” refactors outside admitted paths.
- Re-specifying the entire legacy system as feature `001`.
- Ignoring existing tests and inventing a parallel harness by default.
- Claiming `/pstack:interrogate` consensus when pstack is not installed
  (use native multi-leaf review + record the limit).
- Switching hosts mid-feature without flushing `progress.md` and dirty owners.

---

## 5. Per-host cheat sheet

### 5.1 Cursor

| Item | Value |
|------|--------|
| Skill | `/agentic-sdd` (global `~/.cursor/skills/agentic-sdd`) |
| Spec Kit | `/speckit-*` or project `.cursor/skills/speckit-*` |
| pstack | Official marketplace `pstack` |
| Continuity | `progress.md` `sdd-continue` + stop-hook ([cursor-continuation.md](cursor-continuation.md)) |
| Implement leaves | `poteto-agent` when spawning Task |
| Model sheet | `~/.cursor/rules/pstack-models.mdc` after `/setup-pstack` |

**Cursor-specific:** do not end a turn on a status report while Goal is open.
Keep the critical path in-thread; hook is backup.

### 5.2 Claude Code

| Item | Value |
|------|--------|
| Skill | `/agentic-sdd` or auto from `~/.claude/skills/agentic-sdd` |
| Spec Kit | `/speckit.*` / project `.claude/skills` |
| pstack | User-scope `pstack@pstack-claude` → `/pstack:<skill>` |
| Continuity | `progress.md` + Claude session loop (no Cursor stop-hook) |
| Compact | Flush `progress.md` before `/compact` |
| Model sheet | After `/pstack:setup-pstack` (port-specific path) |

**Detect pstack:**

```bash
claude plugin list | grep pstack
# or in-session: /plugin list
```

If missing: obligations-only; record `pstack: unavailable|claude` once; continue Spec Kit.

### 5.3 Codex

| Item | Value |
|------|--------|
| Skill | `$agentic-sdd` (`agents/openai.yaml`) |
| Spec Kit | `$speckit-*` |
| pstack | Codex plugin from same ports when installed |
| Continuity | File handoff in `progress.md` / feature artifacts |
| Activation | `setup-speckit-multi-agent activate codex --project PATH` before write |

Prefer `$speckit-*` over free-form chat for phase ownership.

### 5.4 Switching hosts mid-feature

1. Flush `progress.md` handoff block (see phase-contract).
2. Capture dirty path owners.
3. `activate` the target host when using the multi-agent helper.
4. Receiving agent verifies snapshot before writing.
5. Never copy specs into a host-only directory.

---

## 6. Shared runtime rules (agents)

1. **Spec Kit order wins** over any pstack playbook.
2. **No free-standing poteto-mode** that replaces phases — apply non-negotiables
   *inside* implement/fix batches (`/poteto-mode` or `/pstack:poteto-mode` skill text).
3. **Breadcrumb** in `progress.md`:

```text
pstack: O-architect|cursor|/architect → plan.md updated
pstack: O-poteto|claude|/pstack:poteto-mode → T012 verified
pstack: unavailable|codex → obligations-only
```

4. **Autonomy:** no phase quiz; reversible forks → recorded default.
5. **Hard boundaries:** destructive, secrets, scope beyond Final Goal, Spec Kit
   extension installs — confirm once / `blocked`.
6. **REA** after clean converge before feature close ([rea-closeout.md](rea-closeout.md)).
7. **Missing pstack ≠ failed SDD.** Continue with obligations.

---

## 7. Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Check | Fix |
|---------|-------|-----|
| Agent asks which phase next | Autonomy grant ignored | Re-invoke `/agentic-sdd`; cite this guide §6 |
| Claude has no `/pstack:*` | User-scope plugin missing | §2.2 Claude install |
| Cursor stops and never resumes | `sdd-continue` missing/stuck | Write machine line; see cursor-continuation |
| Two agents editing same tree | No activate / dirty owners | One writer; activate + flush |
| Brownfield “rewrite everything” | Wrong field type | Re-pin admitted paths; new numbered feature for extras |
| Init on dirty brownfield | `--init-existing` / `--force` | Clean baseline or explicit human authorize |
| Interrogate “consensus” alone | Single model | Record limit; still need Spec Kit evidence |
| Feature CLOSED but Goal open | Normal | specify next numbered feature; no quiz |

---

## 8. Quick decision tree

```text
Is there an application already?
├─ No  → GREENFIELD (§3)
│         Init Spec Kit → /agentic-sdd → full phase chain + pstack map
└─ Yes → BROWNFIELD (§4)
          ├─ .specify/ ok? → B1 continue
          ├─ no .specify/? → B2 human-authorized init, then narrow feature
          ├─ pointer conflict? → B3 reconcile
          └─ broken behavior? → B4 bug workflow
```

Host pick (writer for this session):

```text
Primary daily driver?
├─ Cursor → official pstack + sdd-continue
├─ Claude → user-scope pstack-claude + /pstack:*
└─ Codex  → $agentic-sdd + $speckit-* (+ pstack port if installed)
```

---

## 9. Definition of done

| Audience | Done means |
|----------|------------|
| **Human** | Final Goal observable; can delete the chat and resume from `progress.md` + feature artifacts on any host |
| **Agent** | Spec Kit evidence current; REA disposition `pass` or `not-applicable`; `sdd-continue` / progress status `delivered` (or next feature already started); no open blocking acceptance |

---

## 10. Minimal reference cards

### Greenfield (one screen)

1. `specify init` (+ peer integrations)  
2. `/agentic-sdd` + Final Goal + field greenfield  
3. Phases auto-advance; pstack inside phases  
4. REA → next feature or delivered  

### Brownfield (one screen)

1. Classify B1–B5; never silent whole-app rewrite  
2. Orient (`how`/`why`) → specify **bound** change  
3. Reuse architecture + existing checks  
4. Implement small; blast-radius; interrogate; REA  

### pstack invoke

| Need | Cursor | Claude |
|------|--------|--------|
| Design before code | `/architect` | `/pstack:architect` |
| Bakeoff | `/arena` | `/pstack:arena` |
| Parallel slices | `/swarm` | `/pstack:swarm` |
| Adversarial review | `/interrogate` | `/pstack:interrogate` |
| Batch style | poteto non-negotiables | same via `/pstack:poteto-mode` skill text |

<!-- file: references/starting-tool-considerations.md -->

---
description: Host-specific bootstrap for Spec Kit Agentic SDD on Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, and Grok Build.
---

# Starting Tool Considerations

**Default process is Spec Kit** (`specify → plan → tasks → implement → converge → REA closeout`).
Artifacts and phase contracts do not change by host. Only bootstrap and
invocation syntax change.

Greenfield vs brownfield procedures (with copy/paste prompts): 
[host-guide-greenfield-brownfield.md](host-guide-greenfield-brownfield.md).

Canonical skill path on this machine:

```text
~/.agents/skills/agentic-sdd/
```

Symlinked into Claude, Codex, Cursor, and Grok skill roots. Prefer that shared
copy; do not fork per-agent skill trees.

## Claude Code

| Item | Value |
|------|--------|
| Skill | `~/.claude/skills/agentic-sdd` (symlink) or project `.claude/skills/agentic-sdd` |
| Project rules | `CLAUDE.md` |
| Spec Kit key | `claude` via `setup-speckit-multi-agent` |
| Phase invoke | `/speckit.specify`, `/speckit.plan`, … (installed surface) |
| Compact | `/compact` after flushing `progress.md` |
| Subagents | Native Agent/Task; prefer port poteto agent for implement leaves when pstack is installed |
| pstack | Install port e.g. `michael-denyer/pstack-claude` → `/pstack:<skill>`; map in [pstack-integration.md](pstack-integration.md) |

**First actions**

1. Confirm Spec Kit is installed for this project (`specify` / `.specify/` present).
2. If missing, stop and use `setup-speckit-multi-agent` — do not invent phases.
3. Detect whether Claude pstack plugin is installed (`/pstack:poteto-mode` / plugin list). If yes, use `/pstack:*` per the phase map; if no, obligations-only and record `pstack: unavailable|claude` once.
4. Read active feature + `progress.md`, then run the owning phase command.
5. After each phase stage, update feature artifacts and `progress.md`.
6. Advance to the next Spec Kit phase without a human quiz while Final Goal work remains.
7. Inside `implement` / bug `fix`, apply poteto non-negotiables without replacing Spec Kit order (`/pstack:architect`, `/pstack:arena`, `/pstack:swarm`, `/pstack:interrogate`, …).

## Codex

| Item | Value |
|------|--------|
| Skill | `~/.codex/skills/agentic-sdd` → `~/.agents/skills/agentic-sdd` |
| Project rules | `AGENTS.md` |
| Spec Kit key | `codex` |
| Phase invoke | `$speckit-specify`, `$speckit-plan`, … |
| Agents meta | `agents/openai.yaml` in this skill (`$agentic-sdd`) |
| pstack | Codex plugin from same ports as Claude when installed; else obligations ([pstack-integration.md](pstack-integration.md)) |

**First actions**

1. Load `$agentic-sdd` or follow this `SKILL.md`.
2. Resolve feature via `.specify/feature.json` / inspect report.
3. Prefer `$speckit-*` over free-form chat for phase work.
4. If a Codex pstack port is installed, use its skill names inside phases; otherwise obligations-only.
5. Keep handoffs in files; do not rely on long chat history.

## Cursor

| Item | Value |
|------|--------|
| Skill | `~/.cursor/skills/agentic-sdd` → `~/.agents/skills/agentic-sdd` |
| Project rules | `.cursor/rules/` and/or `AGENTS.md` |
| Spec Kit key | `cursor-agent` |
| Phase invoke | `/speckit.*` or Cursor skill commands as installed |
| Subagents | Task tool; prefer `poteto-agent` for implement leaves when pstack is installed |
| pstack | Marketplace plugin `pstack` — phase map in [pstack-integration.md](pstack-integration.md) |

**First actions**

1. Ensure the agent can see this skill (user/global skills) and detect whether pstack skills are loaded.
2. Run inspect/`sdd` when `setup-speckit-multi-agent` is available.
3. Enter the owning Spec Kit phase; do not recreate plan/tasks as chat-only docs.
4. Parent model stays as the user selected; route Spec Kit phase children from `~/.cursor/rules/pstack-models.mdc` when present, else pstack defaults.
5. A Cursor turn ends when the assistant stops. Do not stop after a status report. A completion notice for one shell or subagent is not a new goal; resume the parent Final Goal. Host compaction resumes from `progress.md`. Before any user-visible status, update the `sdd-continue` line in that file. See [cursor continuation](cursor-continuation.md).
6. If Spec Kit slash commands are not invocable, execute the phase contract against the feature files.
7. Keep the critical path in this turn. Do not hand it to a background subagent and end the turn. A stop-hook follow-up that contains `sdd-continue-followup` is the same Final Goal, not a new task.
8. Inside `implement` / bug `fix`, apply poteto-mode non-negotiables without replacing Spec Kit phase order. Use `/architect`, `/arena`, `/swarm`, `/interrogate`, `/blast-radius` per the obligation table.

## Grok Build

| Item | Value |
|------|--------|
| Skill | `~/.grok/skills/agentic-sdd` → `~/.agents/skills/agentic-sdd` |
| Project rules | Grok project instructions / system prompt |
| Spec Kit key | **None native** — use file-based Spec Kit layout |
| Phase invoke | Follow Spec Kit artifact contracts manually using this skill; `/goal` for the completion condition |
| Models | `grok models` (read-only listing; not a paid probe) |

**First actions**

1. Confirm `.specify/` and the canonical spec root exist (same layout as other hosts).
2. If the project was set up only for Codex/Cursor/Claude, still honor shared
   `.specify/` + `specs/` (or `.specify/specs/`) — do not create a Grok-only fork.
3. Execute phase contracts from [phase-contract.md](phase-contract.md) against
   those files when slash/`$speckit-*` commands are unavailable.
4. Route per `model-routing.md`. pstack loads on Grok through `pstack@pstack-claude` (`grok plugin install pstack@pstack-claude --trust`) or Claude compat scanning; see `pstack-integration.md`. Prefer file handoff over chat memory.

When Spec Kit CLI or agent integrations are missing on Grok, do **not** invent
alternate directories. Either ask the user to run `setup-speckit-multi-agent`
from a supported host, or continue on the existing shared artifacts only.

## Switching hosts mid-feature

1. Flush `progress.md` and feature artifacts (handoff block from phase-contract).
2. Capture HEAD + dirty ownership (`inspect --full` when available).
3. On Codex/Cursor/Claude: `setup-speckit-multi-agent activate <agent>`.
4. Receiving host: verify snapshot before writing; one writer per checkout.

## Universal first steps (any of the four)

1. Detect host → use the table above.
2. Resolve project + active feature + phase (Spec Kit metadata).
3. Read constitution / project instructions + current feature artifacts.
4. Pin Final Goal + verification contract.
5. Run the owning Spec Kit phase (or file-equivalent on Grok).
6. Update `progress.md` after meaningful stages; compact only after flush.

## REA closeout (all four hosts)

After clean converge, run REA before finish. Prefer MCP tools named `rea` /
`user-rea`. If unavailable in delivery/repair closeout only:

```sh
npm install -g rea-agents@6.7.0   # do not upgrade a working CLI
# Pick ONE active-id: cursor | claude_code | codex | grok_build
rea setup --dry-run --yes --client <active-id> --format json
rea setup --yes --client <active-id>
```

`--client claude` / `--client grok` are invalid. Do not use `--all-detected` or
`curl | bash`. Reconnect MCP if needed. Full rules: [rea-closeout.md](rea-closeout.md).

## What does not change

- Spec Kit default workflow and phase ownership
- Shared `.specify/` + canonical spec root
- Hard boundaries for destructive actions, secrets, Spec Kit extension installs
- Narrow REA install/setup for delivery/repair closeout only (see rea-closeout.md)
- Evidence and authorization decide; reviewers advise
- Light path remains opt-in trivial-only

---

<!-- file: references/agent-compatibility.md -->

---
description: Compatibility matrix for Spec Kit Agentic SDD across Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, and Grok Build.
---

# Agent Compatibility

This skill is **Spec Kit–first** and **agent-agnostic on artifacts**. One
`.specify/` tree and one canonical spec root are the source of truth. Hosts are
invocation surfaces only.

## Matrix

| Capability | Claude Code | Codex | Cursor | Grok Build |
|------------|-------------|-------|--------|------------|
| Skill install path | `~/.claude/skills/agentic-sdd` | `~/.codex/skills/agentic-sdd` | `~/.cursor/skills/agentic-sdd` | `~/.grok/skills/agentic-sdd` |
| Shared canon | → `~/.agents/skills/agentic-sdd` | same | same | same |
| Spec Kit `specify` key | `claude` | `codex` | `cursor-agent` | — (file-based) |
| Multi-agent setup helper | yes | yes | yes | consume shared artifacts; activate N/A |
| Phase slash / `$` commands | `/speckit.*` | `$speckit-*` | `/speckit.*` / skills | emulate via files + this skill |
| Subagent model pin | Agent/Task when available | Codex child agents | Cursor Task | Grok subagent / `grok -m` |
| Compaction | `/compact` | host context mgmt + `progress.md` | host context mgmt + `progress.md` | `progress.md` flush + short resume |
| REA closeout | MCP/CLI; `rea setup --yes --client claude_code` | `--client codex` | `--client cursor` | `--client grok_build`; CLI `capture-browser-scenario` if MCP down |
| pstack execution style | `pstack@pstack-claude`: `/pstack:*`, `pstack:poteto-agent[-<level>]` | `pstack@pstack-claude`: skills by name, `spawn_agent` + `reasoning_effort` | Official marketplace `pstack`: `/architect`, `poteto-agent` | `pstack@pstack-claude` (or Claude compat scan): skills by name, `spawn_subagent` |
| Completion goal | `/goal` (transcript-judged Stop-hook evaluator; headless via `claude -p "/goal …"`) | none native → `AGENTS.md` continuity + `progress.md` | `/goal` (`CreateGoal`/`UpdateGoal`, no budget) + `sdd-continue` stop hook | `/goal [--budget <tokens>]` with independent evidence review |

## Requirements for “works”

On every host the agent must be able to:

1. **Read/write** the project workspace (feature specs, plans, tasks, `.specify/`).
2. **Discover** this skill's `SKILL.md` and `references/`.
3. **Run** Python 3.10+ helpers under `scripts/` (stdlib only).
4. **Honor** phase ownership — do not edit code in `converge`, do not tick
   reviewer checklists in `implement`, etc.
5. **Refuse** to create a second per-agent spec tree.

Optional but preferred for delivery mid-flight:

- Spec Kit CLI `specify` ≥ 1.0.1
- `setup-speckit-multi-agent` for setup/inspect/activate/sdd

**Required at closeout:** REA (`user-rea` MCP and/or `rea` CLI from `rea-agents`).
If missing in delivery/repair closeout, install pinned package and
`rea setup --yes --client <active-id>` — see [rea-closeout.md](rea-closeout.md).
`--client claude` / `grok` are invalid; use `claude_code` / `grok_build`.

Missing mid-flight optional tools: continue on shared files with explicit recorded
limits. Do not fake Spec Kit command success. Do not fake REA success.

## Grok-specific notes

- There is no Spec Kit integration key for Grok today. Treat Grok as a first-class
  **consumer** of the same Spec Kit project other hosts set up.
- Point Grok Build project instructions at this skill and the project's
  constitution / `AGENTS.md` / `CLAUDE.md` equivalents.
- Use `grok models` only as a read-only catalog source for routing.
- If slash commands are absent, execute the same phase contracts against files
  and name the phase explicitly in `progress.md`.

## Codex agents metadata

`agents/openai.yaml` enables Codex `$agentic-sdd` invocation. Keep
`allow_implicit_invocation: true` so Spec Kit delivery can attach without a
manual skill quiz when relevant.

## Universal practices

- Prefer updating `spec.md` / `plan.md` / `tasks.md` / `progress.md` / checks
  over chat memory.
- Mid-project host switch: flush handoff → capture dirty owners → activate
  (when supported) → verify snapshot → continue.
- Do not assume vendor slash commands exist; fall back to plain-language phase
  steps that still write Spec Kit artifacts.
- Never lower acceptance to match a defective implementation.
- Delivery/repair via this skill is unattended inside the Final Goal: no phase
  quiz; reversible forks get a recorded default. See [pstack-integration.md](pstack-integration.md).
- pstack never owns Spec Kit artifacts. Cursor uses official `pstack`; Claude/Codex
  use a `/pstack:*` port when installed, else obligations — never claim a skill ran
  that the host cannot invoke.
