<!-- file: references/cursor-continuation.md -->

---
description: Cursor stop-hook resume for an open agentic-sdd Final Goal.
---

# Cursor continuation

Cursor ends a turn when the assistant reply has no further tool call. Prompt rules cannot reopen that turn. A user-level stop hook submits the next user message while the Final Goal is still running.

This file is for Cursor only. Claude Code, Codex, and Grok keep their own loops.

## Machine line

Update this single line in the workspace root `progress.md` before any user-visible status:

```html
<!-- sdd-continue: {"status":"running","stop_reason":null,"next_action":"implement T012"} -->
```

| Field | Values |
|-------|--------|
| `status` | `running`, `delivered`, `blocked` |
| `stop_reason` | `null`, `destructive`, `secret`, `missing_goal`, `contradiction`, `evidence` |
| `next_action` | One concrete Spec Kit step |

Keep the JSON valid and inside one comment. `next_action` is a JSON string.

- While work remains, `status` is `running` and `stop_reason` is `null`.
- When the Final Goal is delivered, set `status` to `delivered` and stop.
- For a destructive action, a secret, a missing or contradictory goal, or an evidence or authority boundary, set `status` to `blocked`, set `stop_reason` to the matching value, and ask once.

`delivered` or `blocked` makes the hook stay silent. A hard `stop_reason` on a `running` line does too.

## What the hook does

Scripts live in `~/.cursor/hooks/agentic-sdd-continue/`. The stop script is last in `~/.cursor/hooks.json` and uses `loop_limit: null`. The script itself allows 80 automatic follow-ups per arm.

- A prompt containing `agentic-sdd` arms the session and clears hold, the follow-up count, and a stuck latch.
- A short resume phrase (`계속`, `이어서 진행`, `continue`, `keep going`, and the close variants in the script) does the same only when the session is already armed.
- Any other human prompt sets hold. The hook does not continue after that answer.
- A follow-up contains the marker `sdd-continue-followup`. That marker clears hold and does not reset the budget. It is the same Final Goal, not a new task.
- Ask mode and background agents are never resumed. Aborted and error stops are never resumed.
- A missing machine line still continues once. The follow-up tells the agent to write the line, then do the next action.
- The same `next_action` and the same `progress.md` modification time on two consecutive stops latches stuck. Only a later human arm clears it.
- Follow-up 80 tells the agent to say the continuation budget is spent if the goal is still open. Follow-up 81 is not sent. A later human `/agentic-sdd` or resume phrase resets the count.

The hook does not approve shell or MCP calls. Those cards still wait for the human.

Cursor has no Skill tool. If `/speckit.*` is not invocable, execute the phase contract against the feature files. Do not hand the critical path to a background subagent and end the turn. The hook is the backup when a turn ends anyway.

## Follow-up shape

The injected message starts with `<!-- sdd-continue-followup -->` and tells the agent to read `progress.md`, do `next_action`, and avoid spending the turn on a status report.

---

<!-- file: references/cost-modes.md -->

---
description: Cost modes for Spec Kit Agentic SDD. Balanced/Thorough stay Spec Kit; Economy only narrows verification and model spend.
---

# Cost Modes

Spec Kit phase ownership does **not** change by cost mode. Modes adjust model
spend, verification breadth, and compaction aggressiveness — not whether
`specify → plan → tasks → implement → converge → REA closeout` applies.
Converged is not finish; only REA `pass` or `not-applicable` finishes.

| Mode | When | Behavior |
|------|------|----------|
| **Economy** | High volume, low risk, explicit budget | Prefer light child models for mechanical leaves; compact early; keep Spec Kit artifacts but narrow intermediate checks |
| **Balanced** | Default | Full Spec Kit core flow; repository checks + narrowest extra proof; pstack-sheet routing at phase/recovery boundaries |
| **Thorough** | High-risk or user asks for high confidence | Full Spec Kit + clarify/analyze/checklist as needed; multi-perspective review at converge; deeper evidence classes |

## Defaults

- Start in **Balanced**.
- Escalate to Thorough for auth, payment, personal data, public API, schema,
  production config, or irreversible multi-module work.
- Economy never skips phase ownership or relaxes acceptance to save tokens.
- Light-path (no full Spec Kit) remains a separate opt-in for trivial work only
  — it is not Economy mode.

## Interaction with pstack panels

See the "Panel size by cost mode" table in `pstack-integration.md`: Economy
runs a 2-reviewer interrogate and skips `architect` on single-file specs;
Thorough keeps the full panel and adds `thermos` where present.

## Interaction with routing

- Economy: bias leaves toward the worker/light model when evidence allows.
- Balanced: use the sheet/default order from `model-routing.md`.
- Thorough: allow escalate-class models when budget remains; still require evidence.

---

<!-- file: references/multi-perspective-review.md -->

---
description: Multi-perspective checklist for Spec Kit converge (or bug test). Not for mid-implement.
---

# Multi-Perspective Review (Converge / Bug Test Only)

Apply at feature `converge` or bug `test` — not during intermediate `implement`
or bug `fix` steps. Use in Thorough mode or when risk warrants it.

## Perspectives

### Product / User Value
- [ ] Acceptance criteria map directly to the user story / Final Goal slice.
- [ ] Happy path and at least one meaningful failure path are observable.
- [ ] No unrequested features were added.

### Engineering Feasibility & Maintainability
- [ ] Change is localized to the admitted scope.
- [ ] New code follows existing patterns (or deviation is justified in progress.md).
- [ ] Dependencies introduced are minimal and justified.

### Security & Permissions
- [ ] No secrets or credentials in code, logs, or progress.md.
- [ ] Auth / data access boundaries are unchanged or explicitly updated and tested.
- [ ] External calls or file system writes stay within approved scope.

### Operations & Reliability
- [ ] Failure modes do not leave the system inconsistent.
- [ ] The change is detectable if it fails later (log, status, or progress.md).
- [ ] Rollback path exists or the change is low-risk and reversible.

### UX / Accessibility / i18n (when relevant)
- [ ] Error / empty states defined for user-visible output.
- [ ] Accessibility or localization impact noted (or explicitly out of scope).

## Usage Rules

- Check only perspectives material to the current feature/bug.
- Record results in `progress.md` under Decisions or Open issues.
- Material gaps → append tasks and return to implement once (one converge per
  spec), or open a sibling
  feature/bug. Do not silently expand or relax acceptance.
- This is a short multi-lens pass, not a substitute for required evidence classes
  in [phase-contract.md](phase-contract.md).
- With pstack on any host: run `interrogate` (`/interrogate` on Cursor,
  `/pstack:interrogate` on Claude, native skill on Codex) — obligation
  `O-interrogate`. Add `thermos` on the Claude/Codex port for auth, payment,
  schema, or public-API changes.
- Reconcile findings into this checklist and `tasks.md`. Interrogate agreement alone
  is not Spec Kit convergence.
- With pstack present, a required review that no independent reviewer can run
  stays `BLOCKED: independent review` (recorded in `progress.md`); the feature
  stays open. Self-review, green tests, or CI do not close it.
- Only if pstack is absent: spawn at least two independent review leaves with
  different models when the host allows; otherwise explicit single-model
  self-review with the limit recorded — never claim multi-model consensus.

---

<!-- file: references/compaction-timing.md -->

---
description: "Optimal timing for context compaction to reduce token cost without losing critical state."
---

# Compaction Timing Guide

## Core Rule

**Compact at logical task boundaries, not only when the context window is almost full.**

Waiting until 80–95% capacity means the model is already working with degraded context. The summary it produces will be based on a partially compressed view.

## Recommended Triggers

| Trigger | When | Why |
|---------|------|-----|
| **Spec Kit phase boundary** (preferred) | After specify/plan/tasks/implement/converge stage, or bug assess/fix/test | State is clean and easy to summarize accurately |
| **~150k–250k tokens** | Mid-session when context has grown but work is still coherent | Avoids quality drop before the hard limit |
| **Before high-risk step** | Before auth changes, schema migrations, or irreversible actions | Ensures the model has a clear, focused context |
| **Idle / session end** | After ~50–60 min idle (Claude Code idle compaction) | Prevents full re-processing when resuming |

## How to Compact Well

1. **Flush durable state first**  
   With pstack present, run the poteto `pause-safely` step first (`O-pause`; `resume.mjs publish` on the Claude/Codex port). Then:  
   Update `progress.md` (Overall status, current scope, completed, next action) and any relevant spec files before compacting.

2. **Give explicit instructions**  
   Do not use a bare `/compact`. Examples:
   - `/compact keep the current goal, acceptance criteria, progress.md summary, and next action`
   - `/compact focus on the auth fix; drop exploration notes`

3. **Prefer short progress.md over long history**  
   After compaction, the next turn should start from the updated `progress.md` rather than relying on the summary alone.

## What to Avoid

- Compacting mid-derivation or mid-search (partial results are lost and must be recomputed).
- Compacting only when the window is nearly full.
- Compacting without first writing key decisions and next actions to disk.
- Using compaction as a substitute for routing simple work to light models (Haiku 5.5 / Luna).

## Interaction with Cost Mode

- **Economy**: Compact earlier and more aggressively. Prefer task-boundary compaction.
- **Balanced**: Compact at logical milestones or around 200k tokens.
- **Thorough**: Compact less frequently, but still at clear stage boundaries. Preserve more intermediate reasoning if it is material.

## Practical Default for This Skill

After every Spec Kit phase stage (or bug stage):

1. Update feature artifacts, then `progress.md` (Overall + next phase action).
2. Compact with an instruction that preserves Final Goal, feature/phase, and next action.
   - Claude Code: `/compact ...`
   - Codex / Cursor / Grok: use host context management; always rely on `progress.md` as the resume surface.
3. Continue from compacted state + `progress.md` + current feature paths.

---

<!-- file: references/bug-workflow.md -->

---
description: Spec Kit bug workflow — assess → fix → test.
---

# Bug Fix Workflow

Use when existing behavior is broken. Do not run the full feature delivery cycle
first unless the "bug" is actually new scope.

Artifacts live in `.specify/bugs/<slug>/`.

Prefer installed commands when present (`speckit.bug.assess` / `.fix` / `.test`
or the project's equivalent). This document is the file contract when those
commands are unavailable (including Grok Build file-based mode).

## Stages

### 1. Assess (no code changes)

With pstack: `how` over the affected subsystem and `why` for regression history
(`O-why`); reproduce on the real surface first. Assessment stays read-only.

- Input: symptom, reproduction, expected vs actual, issue URL / stack trace.
- Output: `.specify/bugs/<slug>/assessment.md`
- Content: verdict (`real` / `invalid` / `needs-clarification`), suspected paths,
  proposed remediation, scope.

### 2. Fix (only stage that edits code)

- Apply only the assessed remediation.
- Stay within listed files unless new evidence requires expansion (log under Deviations).
- Output: `.specify/bugs/<slug>/fix.md`
- Include exact file changes and any added tests.

### 3. Test (no code changes to force pass)

- Re-run original reproduction and relevant tests.
- Output: `.specify/bugs/<slug>/test.md`
- Verdict: `verified` | `partial` | `failed`
- Missing verification is not success. Failed tests return to diagnosis/fix.

## Scaffold helper

```bash
scripts/init-bug-dir.sh <slug> --project /path/to/repo
```

Prefer `specify extension add bug` (user-authorized) via
`setup-speckit-multi-agent --with-bug` when setting up a project.

## Templates

**assessment.md**
```markdown
# Bug Assessment: <slug>

- **Verdict**: real | invalid | needs-clarification
- **Symptom**: 
- **Suspected paths**: 
- **Proposed remediation**: 
- **Scope**: 
```

**fix.md**
```markdown
# Bug Fix: <slug>

- **Status**: applied | partial | not-applied
- **Changes**:
  | File | Change |
  |------|--------|
- **Deviations from Assessment**: 
```

**test.md**
```markdown
# Bug Test: <slug>

- **Verdict**: verified | partial | failed
- **Reproduction result**: 
- **Tests run**: 
- **Evidence**: 
```

## Rules

- Assessment and test are evidence, not permission to edit unrelated files.
- Intermediate checks stay light during Fix; strong verification belongs in Test.
- Update root `progress.md` when a bug is opened or closed.
- Apply [phase-contract](phase-contract.md) verification evidence classes on Test.
- Use [recovery](recovery.md) after two failed Test cycles without new evidence.
- Do **not** write verdict `verified` until REA closeout on the fix surface is
  `pass` or `not-applicable` ([rea-closeout.md](rea-closeout.md)). A material
  REA finding returns to Fix, then Test, then REA on the new code state. Record
  the REA block in `test.md`. Do not append feature `tasks.md` unless the defect
  is new out-of-bug scope.

---

<!-- file: references/anti-patterns.md -->

---
description: Anti-patterns for Spec Kit Agentic SDD.
---

# Anti-Patterns

## Scope & specification

- **Silent expansion**: Adding features or edge cases outside the current feature
  without a new numbered feature or explicit authorization.
- **Inventing requirements**: Filling missing acceptance criteria instead of
  recording an assumption or entering `clarify`.
- **One giant feature**: Combining independent journeys into one feature directory.
- **Second spec store**: Copying specs into agent-specific folders (Claude-only,
  Codex-only, etc.) instead of shared Spec Kit roots.
- **Chat-only phases**: Planning or tasking only in conversation without writing
  `plan.md` / `tasks.md`.

## Verification

- **Over-verification loop**: Full acceptance suite after every tiny edit mid-implement.
- **Test masking**: Skipping or weakening tests to get green.
- **Done without evidence**: Declaring complete when required checks were not run
  on the relevant code state.
- **Converge edits code**: Using converge to patch source instead of appending tasks.
## Handoff & hosts

- **Chat memory reliance**: Decisions never written to feature artifacts / `progress.md`.
- **Stale progress.md**: Stage finished without Overall + next action.
- **Ignoring host bootstrap**: Assuming `/speckit.*` exists on Grok, or inventing
  Grok-only directories.
- **Multi-writer checkout**: Two hosts editing the same feature without handoff.

## Process

- **Skipping Spec Kit by default**: Using light-path for non-trivial work.
- **Self-approving reviewer checklists**: Implementation ticking reviewer-owned markers.
- **Destructive action without confirmation**: Force push, drop tables, secret handling.
- **Blind retry**: Same failing check twice with no new diagnosis or inputs.
- **Setup from delivery skill**: Initializing Spec Kit from this skill instead of
  `setup-speckit-multi-agent`.
- **Skipping or faking REA:** Feature/Final Goal/bug `verified` without a real
  evidence id; URL-only capture counted as pass; `blocked-limitation` used to
  finish; placeholder `ev_…`; refusing to install `rea-agents` when closeout is
  in scope; using `--client claude`/`grok` or `--all-detected`/`curl|bash` against
  the closeout install rules.

## Recovery

When an anti-pattern is detected:

1. Stop the current mutating step if ownership/authority is unclear.
2. Record the anti-pattern under Open issues in `progress.md`.
3. Reverse unsafe changes when safe, or open a bug/feature for correction.
4. Set one concrete next Spec Kit phase action before continuing.

---

<!-- file: references/anti-oververification.md -->

---
description: Prevent infinite verification loops during Spec Kit implement; full proof at converge / bug test.
---

# Anti-Over-Verification Rules

## Core principle

Verification intensity must match the Spec Kit phase. Intermediate `implement`
steps record status for the changed task. Full acceptance evidence belongs at
`converge` (features) or bug `test` (repairs).

## Allowed during implement

- Record pass / fail / unresolved for the 1–2 most relevant acceptance IDs of
  the current task.
- Note open questions in `progress.md`.
- Continue to the next admitted task when blockers are recorded.
- Reuse still-valid passing evidence after unrelated edits.

## Forbidden during implement

- Re-running the full acceptance suite after every small change without new risk.
- Expanding the current feature to absorb mid-flight edge cases (split / new feature).
- Looping the same check until perfect before any progress (use verification_guard).
- Treating converge as a coding phase.

## Final verification (converge / bug test)

- Only after current tasks (or bug fix) are done.
- Check every required acceptance criterion for that feature/bug.
- Unmet gaps stay open: append tasks and return to implement (features) or fix (bugs).
  Do not accept residual gaps to get green.
- After a clean converge (or bug test evidence, before writing `verified`), run
  mandatory [REA closeout](rea-closeout.md). Write feature close / `verified`
  only when REA disposition is `pass` or `not-applicable`.

## Guard helper

After two unchanged attempts of the same check:

```bash
python scripts/verification_guard.py ...
```

See [verification-execution.md](verification-execution.md).

## Split triggers

Stop and split (new numbered feature or sibling bug) if:

- Intermediate verification time exceeds implementation time.
- Spec exceeds size guidance (`scripts/check-spec-size.sh`).
- The agent revisits the same criteria without new evidence.

---

<!-- file: references/edge-cases-and-failure-modes.md -->

---
description: Edge cases and recovery patterns for Spec Kit Agentic SDD.
---

# Edge Cases & Failure Modes

## Classification ambiguity

Under `/agentic-sdd` delivery/repair, prefer a recorded default over a quiz.
Ask once and set `blocked` only when two readings imply incompatible Final Goals
and artifacts/user text give no dominant reading — or when a hard boundary applies.

| Situation | Action |
|-----------|--------|
| Request mixes new feature + bug fix | Pick primary from wording + evidence (fix if existing behavior is broken; else feature). Record assumption in `progress.md`. Ask only if both readings are equally strong and incompatible |
| No clear acceptance | Enter `clarify`; derive 1–2 observable outcomes from repo + Final Goal; record as assumptions — do not invent product scope. Block only if no observable outcome can be stated |
| User says "just do it" / full autonomy | Still use Spec Kit for non-trivial work; list assumptions in Notes; no phase quiz |
| Requirements change mid-implement | New numbered feature or bug — do not silently expand current feature |
| Trivial typo/docs-only | Opt-in light path only (see SKILL.md); otherwise full Spec Kit |

## Partial failure & recovery

- **Interrupted write**: Record intended change set in `progress.md` before multi-file edits. On resume, verify what landed.
- **Tool failure mid-step**: Record exact error, last good path, next safe action. Do not retry unchanged.
- **progress.md missing**: Recreate from feature artifacts + git status; note handoff loss.
- **Conflicting instructions**: Prefer current feature artifacts > `progress.md` > project instructions; ask if unclear.
- **Flaky check**: Mark unresolved; do not loop. Full investigation at converge / bug test.
- **Host switch mid-feature**: Flush handoff, capture dirty owners, activate when supported, verify snapshot.

## Spec Kit / host gaps

- **No Spec Kit installed**: Stop mutating; point user to `setup-speckit-multi-agent`.
- **Grok without slash commands**: Execute phase contracts on shared files; name the phase in `progress.md`.
- **Integration missing for one host**: Do not fork specs; use shared `.specify/` only.
- **Branch vs feature mismatch**: Reconcile pointer before continuing (see setup skill `sdd` report).

## Security & destructive operations

- Never commit secrets. Stop and report the path if discovered.
- Destructive ops require explicit confirmation in the current session; record it.
- External network / publish steps must be in-scope or explicitly approved.
- When permission is unclear, stop affected mutation and ask.

## Multi-perspective gaps (at converge)

Briefly note status against:

- User value vs acceptance
- Security / permissions
- Failure states
- Observability
- Reversibility

Unknown material items become open issues — not silent passes.

## When to stop and ask

- Classification still ambiguous after reading context.
- Change touches paths outside admitted scope.
- Required evidence blocked by missing credentials/external systems.
- Same bounded step failed twice without new evidence.
- Prior rejection of a similar approach is recorded.

Do not quiz on every small reversible decision; record assumptions and continue.

---

<!-- file: references/main-model-guide.md -->

---
description: Main vs light model roles for Spec Kit Agentic SDD; token overuse causes and fixes.
---

# Main Model Setting Guide

The **parent** model is the user's choice. This guide covers child routing and
common token waste. The pstack sheet and skill defaults decide concrete slugs — see
[model-routing.md](model-routing.md).

## Role of the main (parent) model

Use a capable parent for Spec Kit coordination:

| Host family | Strong parent defaults (when available) | Cost-conscious |
|-------------|------------------------------------------|----------------|
| Claude | Opus-class | Sonnet-class |
| OpenAI | Sol-class | — |
| xAI / Grok | Grok 4.7+ | — |
| Gemini | Argon-class | — |

Do not set Astra or Terra as the default parent on this machine's GPT-6 policy
unless the user explicitly overrides.

## Light models are for leaves

Haiku-class, Luna-class, Composer/Spark-class, etc. are for **sub-tasks**:

- Classification, extraction, summarization
- Mechanical edits inside an admitted task
- High-volume repetitive work

They are not the Spec Kit orchestrator for multi-phase delivery.

## Why the main model consumes too many tokens

1. Reloading this entire skill + all references every turn.
2. Parent doing mechanical work instead of delegating leaves.
3. Full verification after every micro-edit mid-implement.
4. Uncompacted history; `progress.md` not used as resume surface.
5. Thorough/multi-perspective review on low-risk features.
6. Giant specs that must be re-read constantly.

## Practical fixes

- Keep the active prompt short: Final Goal, phase, hard boundaries, pointer to
  `progress.md` + current feature paths.
- Load references conditionally (see INDEX.md).
- Delegate mechanical leaves; keep parent on phase ownership and integration.
- Intermediate checks stay narrow; full evidence at converge / bug test.
- After each Spec Kit stage: update artifacts → update `progress.md` → compact
  if the host supports it.
- Prefer splitting oversized features over expanding one giant `spec.md`.

---

<!-- file: references/progress-template.md -->

# progress.md Template

Update this file after every meaningful stage.

```markdown
# Progress

## Overall
[auth: done] → [dashboard: in progress] → [notifications: waiting] | Bugs: login-crash (assessed)

## Scope for this session
[Feature dir + Spec Kit phase, or bug slug + assess|fix|test]

## Current outputs
- [path/to/file] — [short status]

## Completed
- [item] — [observed result or check status]

## Decisions
- [choice] — [brief evidence or reason]

## Open issues
- [issue] — [severity / blocker?]

## Next action
[One concrete Spec Kit phase step or bug stage]

## Last updated
[YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM]
```

Rules:
- Always keep the Overall line up to date (features + open bugs + phase).
- Keep the next action singular and Spec Kit–phase actionable.
- Reference exact file paths under the canonical spec root / `.specify/`.
- On host switches, include the handoff block from phase-contract.md.

<!-- file: references/spec-template.md -->

---
description: "Fallback spec shape when the project Spec Kit template is unavailable. Prefer .specify/templates/spec-template.md."
---

# Small Spec Template

Prefer the project's `.specify/templates/spec-template.md` (Given/When/Then).
Use this only when that template is missing. `criterion_gate.py` extracts
English Given/When/Then scenarios, so numbered-only criteria will not score.

```markdown
# [Feature Name]

## Goal
One or two sentences describing the user-facing outcome.

## User Stories
- As a [role], I want [capability] so that [benefit].

## Acceptance Scenarios
1. **Given** [state], **When** [action], **Then** [observable result]
2. **Given** [state], **When** [action], **Then** [observable result]
(Maximum 5. Prefer fewer, precise criteria.)

## Out of Scope
- Explicitly list what this spec will not cover.
- Link to sibling specs if the work was split.

## Notes
- Dependencies or assumptions
- Links to related specs
```

## Quality Checks Before Approving a Spec
- Each acceptance criterion can be turned into a concrete test or observable check.
- Out-of-scope is explicit.
- The spec does not contain implementation details unless they are hard constraints.
- Length stays within 1–3 pages / ≤7 criteria. If larger, split.

## Splitting Guidance
When a feature is large:
1. Identify independent user journeys or bounded capabilities.
2. Create a new numbered spec directory for each.
3. Cross-link them in the Notes section.
4. Implement one small spec at a time.

---

<!-- file: references/overview-template.md -->

---
description: "Human-readable overview spec that maps all child specs so neither agent nor user loses context."
connections: [spec-template, progress-template]
---

# Overview Spec Template

Keep `specs/000-overview/spec.md` short (under 1 page). It is the map, not a detailed spec.

```markdown
# Project Overview

## Overall Goal
[1–2 sentences]

## Child Specs
- [001-auth](../001-auth/spec.md) — Login and session handling
- [002-dashboard](../002-dashboard/spec.md) — Main dashboard after login
- [003-notifications](../003-notifications/spec.md) — In-app notifications

## Current Status
See root `progress.md` Overall line.

## Notes
- Split from original large spec on YYYY-MM-DD
```

## Rules
- Update this file whenever a new child spec is created or a split happens.
- Every child spec must start with a parent link:
  ```markdown
  > Parent: [000-overview](../000-overview/spec.md) | Purpose: [one line]
  ```
- Do not put detailed acceptance criteria here.

<!-- file: references/kanban-board.md -->

---
description: Optional Kanban view over Spec Kit feature and bug artifacts.
---

# Kanban Board

## Purpose

Visual progress over existing Spec Kit artifacts — no separate board file.

Reads:

- `specs/*/spec.md` and/or `.specify/specs/*/spec.md`
- sibling `tasks.md` for feature column movement
- `.specify/bugs/*/` for bug columns
- root `progress.md` Overall line

## Columns

### Features

- **Specified** — spec exists, no checked tasks
- **In Progress** — some tasks checked
- **Done** — all tasks checked

### Bugs

- **Assessed** — `assessment.md` exists
- **Fixed** — fix applied
- **Verified** / **Failed** — from `test.md`

## How agents update

Update normal Spec Kit artifacts (`tasks.md`, bug stage files, `progress.md`).
Do not maintain a parallel board document unless the user wants a text fallback.

## Running the visualizer

The skill is usually installed outside the project. Always pass the project root:

```bash
python ~/.agents/skills/agentic-sdd/visualizer/server.py --project /path/to/repo
```

Or:

```bash
export AGENTIC_SDD_PROJECT=/path/to/repo
python ~/.agents/skills/agentic-sdd/visualizer/server.py
```

Open http://127.0.0.1:8765

Works the same from Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, and Grok Build terminals.

## Lightweight alternative (no server)

In `progress.md`:

```markdown
## Board
- Specified: 001-auth
- In Progress: 002-export
- Done: 000-overview
- Bugs: login-crash (assessed)
```

<!-- file: references/provider-personas-and-docs.md -->

description: "How to use provider personas and official documentation as tools."
---

# Provider Personas and Official Docs as Tools

## Provider Personas

Load the appropriate persona when the work is provider-specific:

| Provider | Persona File | Preferred Main Model | Light Model |
|----------|--------------|----------------------|-------------|
| Anthropic | `personas/anthropic.md` | Sonnet 5.5 / Opus 5.5 | Haiku 5.5 |
| OpenAI | `personas/openai.md` | GPT-6.1 Sol / GPT-6 Sol | GPT-6 Luna |
| Google | `personas/google.md` | Gemini 4 Argon | — |
| xAI | `personas/xai.md` | Grok 4.7+ | — |

**Excluded**: GPT-6 Astra, any Terra variant.

## Official Docs as Tools

When the task involves a specific provider’s API, model behavior, effort settings, or tooling:

1. Prefer fetching the current official documentation over relying on training data.
2. Use available tools (web fetch, browser, or MCP docs servers if configured).
3. Summarize only the relevant points into `progress.md` or the current spec. Do not leave full doc pages in context.
4. If the documentation cannot be fetched, explicitly note the limitation and fall back to known stable behavior.

### Key Documentation Entry Points

- Anthropic: https://platform.claude.com/docs
- OpenAI: https://developers.openai.com/api/docs
- Google: https://ai.google.dev/docs
- xAI: https://docs.x.ai

## Multi-Agent Usage

When spawning sub-agents:

- Assign the light model (Haiku 5.5 or GPT-6 Luna) for classification, extraction, and simple edits.
- Load the matching provider persona only when the sub-task is provider-specific.
- The main orchestrator should remain on Sonnet 5.5 or Sol unless higher confidence is required.

---
extends: feature, bug-fix
when: Any feature, bug, or multi-file change in a repository that has a Spec Kit `.specify/` directory, or any request that names agentic-sdd, Spec Kit, a numbered feature, or a Final Goal.

# agentic-sdd (Spec Kit owns the phases)

This repository runs Spec Kit through the `agentic-sdd` skill. pstack playbooks
execute *inside* an admitted Spec Kit phase; they do not replace
`specify → plan → tasks → implement → converge → REA closeout`.

- **Before** "`how` over the affected subsystem." resolve the Spec Kit project
  (nearest `.specify/`), the active numbered feature, and its phase from the
  feature artifacts and `progress.md`. Load the `agentic-sdd` skill and its
  `references/pstack-integration.md`. If the phase is not `implement`, hand
  off to the owning Spec Kit phase command and stop this playbook here; the
  phase's own obligation (`O-architect`, `O-interrogate`, …) runs pstack skills
  from there. If the phase is `implement`, continue the Feature playbook as the
  `O-poteto` batch for the admitted task IDs only, with `tasks.md` as the todo
  source of truth.
- **Before** "Reproduce it yourself on the matching surface via the driver skill" resolve the
  Spec Kit bug slug under `.specify/bugs/<slug>/` and its stage
  (`assess` / `fix` / `test`). Assessment writes no code: run `how` and `why`
  (`O-why`) and stop this playbook after `assessment.md` is written. Only the
  `fix` stage continues the Bug fix playbook, scoped to the assessed paths.
- **Before** "Run **Opening a PR**." record `pstack: O-poteto|<host>|<skill> → <task ids> verified`
  in `progress.md`, then return to the Spec Kit sequence: `converge` (with
  `O-blast`, `O-hygiene`, `O-interrogate`), then REA closeout. Open the PR only
  when the Final Goal or the repository's commit policy says so; stop this
  playbook here.

---

<!-- file: templates/cursor-rules/agentic-sdd.mdc -->

---
description: Spec Kit owns the phases; pstack playbooks run inside an admitted phase
alwaysApply: true
---

# agentic-sdd (Spec Kit owns the phases)

This repository runs Spec Kit through the `agentic-sdd` skill. The Cursor pstack
plugin cannot invoke `poteto-mode` on its own and has no project playbooks, so
this rule carries the handoffs that `.agents/playbooks/agentic-sdd.md` provides
on the pstack-claude port.

- Any feature, bug, or multi-file change here, or any request naming agentic-sdd,
  Spec Kit, a numbered feature, or a Final Goal: open the `agentic-sdd` skill
  first, resolve the nearest `.specify/`, the active numbered feature, and its
  phase from the feature artifacts and `progress.md`. A contained one-file edit
  with an obvious check (a typo, a one-line fix) needs none of this: do it
  directly and verify on the real artifact.
- Before a pstack Feature playbook's `how` step: if the phase is not `implement`,
  hand off to the owning Spec Kit phase command and stop the playbook; the
  phase's own obligation (`O-architect`, `O-interrogate`, …) runs pstack skills
  from there. If the phase is `implement`, continue the Feature playbook as the
  `O-poteto` batch for the admitted task IDs only, with `tasks.md` as the todo
  source of truth.
- Before a pstack Bug fix playbook's reproduce step: resolve the Spec Kit bug
  slug under `.specify/bugs/<slug>/` and its stage (`assess` / `fix` / `test`).
  Assessment writes no code: run `how` and `why` and stop after
  `assessment.md`. Only the `fix` stage continues the playbook, scoped to the
  assessed paths.
- Before "Run Opening a PR": record `pstack: O-poteto|cursor|<skill> → <task ids>
  verified` in `progress.md`, then return to Spec Kit: `converge` (with
  `O-blast`, `O-hygiene`, `O-interrogate`), then REA closeout. Open the PR only
  when the Final Goal or the repository's commit policy says so.
- Read `poteto-mode/SKILL.md` from the pstack plugin as a reference for the
  non-negotiables and principles; the model cannot invoke that skill here, the
  user can with `/poteto-mode`.

---

<!-- file: docs/BENCHMARKS.md -->

# Benchmarks

What was measured, how, and what each host actually did at every Spec Kit gate.
All numbers come from files and transcripts (`docs/evals/*/measure*.py`), never
from an agent's own summary. One run per cell (n=1); treat differences under
about 2× as noise.

- Machine: one Mac (macOS 26.6.2, Command Line Tools 26.6, Node 24, Python 3.14), 2026-10-19/20.
- Hosts: Claude Code 2.1.30x (`claude -p`), Codex CLI 0.162 (`codex exec -m gpt-6-luna`), Cursor Agent CLI 2026.10.18 (`agent -p`, composer), Grok Build 1.0.55 (`grok -p`, grok-4.7-build).
- Stack: Spec Kit 1.0.1 project scaffold, pstack-claude 0.9.92–0.9.94 / Cursor pstack 0.15.28, rea-agents 6.7.0, this skill at the commit under test.
- Cost mode: Economy (single-file `O-architect` is n/a, two-reviewer interrogate, prose obligations inline).
- Project: a stdlib Python `todo` CLI (add / list / done, JSON store) that feature 001 had already delivered and closed with REA.

Reproduce: `docs/evals/2026-10-20-host-matrix/tier1.sh`, `tier2.sh`, `tier3.sh`
run the prompts; `measure_tier1.py` and `measure_tier2.py` judge the results.
Raw transcripts are not committed; `artifacts/<host>/progress.md` and the
`converge.md` files are.

## 1. Routing: does the right thing fire at the right size?

Four plan-only prompts per host ("list what you would invoke, then stop").
✔ = matches the expected route, ✘ = does not.

| Prompt | Expected | Claude Code | Codex | Cursor (with project rule) | Grok Build (with home-rule handoffs) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| T: fix a typo in one file | nothing | none ✔ | none ✔ | `agentic-sdd; surgical-patch`, no cycle (mild over-pick) | none ✔ |
| F: add `todo edit` with tests | agentic-sdd → Spec Kit phases, poteto only inside `O-poteto` | ✔ (recall/sharpen → how → specify → plan+architect → tasks → implement leaf → converge once → REA) | ✔ (skill-harness → poteto-mode → agentic-sdd → project playbook → phases) | ✔ (same chain, `tdd` inside the batch) | ✔ (skill-harness → agentic-sdd → phase map) |
| B: intermittent `done` bug | agentic-sdd bug path: assess (how, why) → fix → test → REA | ✔ | ✔ | ✔ (after the rule; before it, stalled in plan mode) | ✔ (after the handoffs; before them, poteto Bug fix only ✘) |
| D: replace JSON with SQLite? | investigate / how / architect, no implement | ✔ | ✔ | ✔ (after the rule; before it, other skill packs + a stale Jev rule ✘) | ✔ |

Reading: no host over-invoked on the trivial task, and all four put the
feature through Spec Kit with poteto inside `O-poteto`. The two misroutes were
both missing-mandate problems (Cursor has no mandate hook; Grok's rule lacked
the Spec Kit handoffs) and both were fixed by the installer's templates.

## 2. Gate by gate: one real feature (`todo edit <id> <text>`)

Each cell is what the host's own `progress.md` breadcrumb says it did at that
gate. "skill" means the named pstack skill or agent actually ran; "inline"
means the lead performed the obligation itself (Economy allows this for prose
and single-file gates); "n/a" is a recorded skip with a reason.

| Gate (obligation) | Claude Code | Codex | Cursor | Grok Build |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Enter: probe + breadcrumbs | `harness: L1 gap, L4 gap, rest ok`, `hook-mandate → satisfied by O-poteto` | probe run, L1 gap, mandate satisfied inside Spec Kit | `harness: all ok`, `pstack: 0.15.28` | `harness: L1 gap, rest ok`, `pstack: 0.9.93` |
| `O-sharpen` | inline (sharpen + in-your-own-words), AC-6/7 pinned | skill gate 0.99 → Final Goal pinned | inline, AC pinned | `sharpen` skill, AC pinned |
| `O-specify` | inline (no technical-writing/unslop run), assumptions as assumptions | spec + requirements checklist reviewed | inline | `technical-writing` + `unslop` skills |
| `O-how` | inline file:line read → `plan.md §Context` | (folded into specify) | inline → `plan.md §Context` | `poteto-agent` explainer → `plan.md §Context` |
| `O-architect` | n/a single-file (Economy) | n/a single-file (Economy) | n/a single-file (Economy) | two `poteto-agent` runners, A base, B rejected |
| `O-sequence` | principle applied, each task ends in a check | 3 ordered tasks | principle applied, T001–T002 | principle applied, 5 tasks |
| `O-poteto` (implement) | `pstack:poteto-agent-low` on sonnet, worktree, cherry-picked; lead review | `spawn_agent` delegates; native reviewer role rejected `gpt-6.1-sol`, general agent used | leaf **unavailable (usage limit)** → parent implemented, recorded | `poteto-agent` in a worktree; parent integrated the diff |
| `O-blast` | inline: unknown-id edit leaves store byte-identical | inline: unknown id returns before `save`, bytes compared | inline: exit 1, bytes equal | `blast-radius` skill, level-4 proof incl. missing-file case |
| `O-hygiene` | inline: 0 comments | read-only deslop pass: no findings | inline: no narrating comments | (not recorded for 002) |
| `O-interrogate` | 2× `pstack:effort-low` (opus, haiku) → 1 act-on → T004 | 2 reviewers (`gpt-6-luna@low`, `gpt-5.6-terra@low`), no findings | 2 seats, both `inherit` (second family on limit) → 1 act-on → T003 | 2 `poteto-agent` reviewers, no findings |
| Converge | once; T004 implemented by the lead; no second converge | once; criterion gate `advance=true` 11/11 | once; T003 implemented; no second converge | once; tasks unchanged |
| `O-rea` | MCP 6.7.0 pass `ev_d529d796…` | 3 captures, pass, `evidence/rea.json` | MCP pass `ev_7c5263c4…` | MCP pass `ev_145d76d8…` |
| `O-reflect` | skipped (optional, no repeated mistake) | – | – | – |
| `ROUTING:` lines | 1 (requested vs observed per role) | 0 in line form (prose) | 2 | 3 (`model unpinned, observed unknown`) |

Outcome of the same feature on each host:

| Measure | Claude Code | Codex | Cursor | Grok Build |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Tasks done | 4/4 | 3/3 | 3/3 | 5/5 |
| Black-box: edit / list shows new / unknown id fails | ✔ ✔ ✔ | ✔ ✔ ✔ | ✔ ✔ ✔ | ✔ ✔ ✔ |
| Own test suite | 18 OK | OK | 18 OK | 17 OK |
| Converge count | 1 | 1 | 1 | 1 |
| REA Evidence ids | 1 | 3 | 1 | 4 |
| Commits added | 6 | 10 | 9 | 6 |
| Wall | 519 s | 582 s | 521 s (453 s rerun) | 1997 s |
| Cost | $7.49 | subscription | subscription | $7.15 |
| Top-level turns | 11 | – | – | 77 |

## 3. Gate by gate: a three-part goal with the split rule

Goal: priorities, due dates, `list --sort due|priority`, `list --overdue`,
lossless migration of existing stores, tests. Rule: split when a task list
would exceed about twelve; one converge per spec; carry over instead of
reconverging.

| | Claude Code | Codex | Cursor | Grok Build |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Split decision | 002 priority+due → 003 sort+overdue, "by dependency" | one spec, 7 tasks ("below the threshold") | 002 → 003, same split as Claude | 002 priority+migration → 003 due → 004 sort+overdue, "combined list would pass 12" |
| `O-architect` | n/a single-file, both specs | n/a | n/a | n/a, all three |
| `O-how` | lead read, file:line cited, both specs | (in plan) | (in plan) | `how` explainer, all three |
| `O-poteto` | `pstack:poteto-agent-medium` sonnet, worktree; lead fixed a date-validation gap after review | worker rejected `gpt-6.1-sol` → lead wrote in an isolated branch | leaf unavailable (usage limit) → parent | `poteto-agent` worktree leaves, 26 → 38 → 45 tests |
| `O-blast` | 002: cross-version store round trip proven by run; 003: ISO-order premise checked on 2000 dates | caller census + legacy-store tests against the real executable | – | `blast-radius` level-4 script per spec, `BLAST_OK` |
| `O-hygiene` | 0 comments, both specs | deslop pass clean | – | `comment-sicko`, 0 kills, all three |
| `O-interrogate` | 2× `effort-medium` (opus, haiku): 002 one must-fix (padded / non-ASCII dates) → T008; 003 test gap → T006 | 2 reviewers: one LOW coverage gap → T008 | 2 seats unavailable → lead dual-perspective, clean | 2 `poteto-agent` reviewers, no findings, all three |
| Converge | 1 + 1, fix rounds implemented, no reconverge | 1, "do not reconverge" | 1 + 1 clean | 1 + 1 + 1 clean |
| `O-rea` | pass ×2 (`ev_ae808042…`, `ev_3ee0707c…`) | pass ×2 (first capture excluded: `/bin/sh` digest did not bind to `todo`; direct capture passed) | pass ×2 | pass ×3 |
| Carryover | none | none | none | none |
| Tests / `todo` lines | 28 / 110 | OK / 116 | OK / 131 | OK / 141 |
| Black-box (same script) | all ✔, invalid input exit 2 | all ✔, legacy item gets default `[P3]` | all ✔, invalid priority exit 1 | all ✔, `--sort priority` ties by id |
| Wall / cost | 1151 s, $12.07 | 643 s | 426 s | 5113 s, $17.65, 123 turns |

Reading: every host met the goal with one converge per spec and real
Evidence; the split rule produced three valid shapes (one, two, three specs).
Each extra spec pays the whole gate overhead, which is why Grok's three-spec
run cost more than Claude's two-spec run. Split by dependency, not by count.

## 4. Spec Kit alone versus this stack (A/B, 2026-10-19)

Same brief (the original `todo` CLI, AC-1..AC-5), same scaffold, same model
(Claude Code, opus), both unattended. Arm A: Spec Kit commands only. Arm B:
this skill with pstack obligations and REA closeout.

| Measure | A: Spec Kit alone | B: Spec Kit + agentic-sdd + pstack |
|---|---|---|
| Black-box AC-1..4 | all pass | all pass |
| Own tests | 6 | 15 |
| Corrupt store `{"oops":1}` | Python traceback | `todo: cannot read …: not a todo store`, exit 1 |
| Unwritable path | traceback | `todo: cannot write …`, exit 1 |
| Independent review | none | 4-model interrogate → 4 act-on tasks; blast-radius level-4 proof; second-model re-review |
| Resumable `progress.md` | none | 8 sections, 16 breadcrumbs, `Next action` |
| REA closeout | not attempted | attempted; blocked by a host toolchain defect, later passed after the fix |
| Turns / wall / cost | 21 / 135 s / $0.96 | 24 / 582 s / $11.24 |

Reading: on a 60-line feature the stack found and fixed three defects A
shipped and left an audit trail, for roughly an order of magnitude more
money. The per-feature fixed cost (probe, sharpen, how, architect, interrogate,
REA) is about constant, so the trade improves as the feature grows.

## 5. What the numbers say about the design

1. **Gates are followed, not just listed.** On every host the `progress.md`
   breadcrumbs name the gate, the host, what ran (skill, agent, or inline),
   and the artifact it changed; the converge files and Evidence ids match.
2. **Economy mode is cheap in the right places.** Prose gates and single-file
   architecture went inline on Claude, Codex, and Cursor without losing the
   black-box result; Grok chose to run the skills and paid for it in wall time.
3. **Degradation is explicit.** Cursor's usage limit and Codex's rejected model
   slug both show up as `observed: unavailable` / substitution notes rather
   than as silent success.
4. **One converge is enough when the review is independent.** Every act-on
   finding came from a second reviewer; the fix rounds closed them; no run
   needed a carryover spec.
5. **REA is the only gate that produces evidence a reader can replay.** All
   eleven feature closures across the three tiers carry an `ev_…` id.

## 6. Known limits of these measurements

- n=1 per cell; wall time includes network and plugin cold starts.
- Subscription hosts report no dollar cost.
- Cursor ran under an account usage limit the whole day, so its non-default
  model seats never ran; its numbers are the degraded path.
- Codex wrote prose breadcrumbs rather than the line form, so its gate rows
  above were read from prose by hand.
- Grok ran with no model sheet, so every `ROUTING:` line reads `observed unknown`.
- REA closeouts were process captures of a source-only CLI; no compiled
  artifact was analysed.

---

<!-- file: docs/evals/2026-10-20-host-matrix/result.md -->

# Host matrix result: agentic-sdd + pstack + seven layers on Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Grok

Run 2026-10-20 on one Mac (macOS 26.6.2, CLT 26.6, rea-agents 6.7.0). Judged from
transcripts and files (`measure_tier1.py`, `measure_tier2.py`), never from the
agent's own summary. n=1 per cell; headless drivers only, so interactive-only
behaviour (Cursor plan mode, Codex `/hooks` trust) is reported as a limit.

## Tier 0, static

| Check | Claude | Codex | Cursor | Grok |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `harness_probe.py` (sandbox) | L1 gap, L4 gap, rest ok | all ok except L1 | all ok except L1 | all ok except L1 |
| pstack root found | port 0.9.92 | port 0.9.94 | official 0.15.28 | port 0.9.93 via `[compat.claude]` |
| Mandate visible to the model (headless quote) | yes, "You have pstack." (hook) | yes after the `AGENTS.md` block; the plugin hook never ran under `codex exec` (untrusted) | **no mechanism**; `poteto-mode` is `disable-model-invocation: true` | yes (home rule) |
| Project playbook validates (`check-playbooks.mjs`) | yes | yes | script absent; plugin has no project playbooks; Bug fix step 1 text differs ("control skill") | yes (port) |
| REA MCP 6.7.0 capture | pass `ev_05f218af…`, `ev_7cd25a9a…` | server spawns 6.7.0 (`codex exec`) | server spawns 6.7.0 after restart | server spawns 6.7.0 (`grok -p`) |

Fixes landed from Tier 0: Codex mandate moved into `~/.codex/AGENTS.md`;
`templates/cursor-rules/agentic-sdd.mdc` + `install.sh --project` for Cursor;
`references/poteto-mode-anatomy.md` documents the per-host call chain. L1 gap is
the sandbox (no CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md), L4 gap on Claude is no permission rules in
the sandbox; both are outside the Final Goal of the test project.

## Tier 1, routing (plan only, 4 prompts × 4 hosts)

Prompts: T typo in one file; F multi-file feature (`todo edit`); B intermittent
unknown-cause bug; D design question (JSON vs SQLite). Expected: T → nothing;
F → agentic-sdd + Spec Kit phases, poteto via `O-poteto`; B → agentic-sdd bug
path (assess → how/why → fix) or poteto Bug fix; D → investigation / how /
architect, no implement.

| Host | T | F | B | D |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Claude | none ✔ | agentic-sdd → recall/sharpen → how → specify (technical-writing+unslop) → plan+architect → tasks+sequence → implement O-poteto (`poteto-agent-medium`, worktree) → converge once → REA ✔; opened `agentic-sdd.md`, `pstack-integration.md`, `rea-closeout.md`, `cost-modes.md` | agentic-sdd repair mode, bug extension absent → file-contract scaffold, assess: how + why + reproduce, then fix stage ✔ | memory → agentic-sdd → poteto-mode router → sharpen/why/how/attack-the-premise/blast-radius; architect/interrogate only if "yes" ✔ |
| Codex | none ✔ | skill-harness → poteto-mode → agentic-sdd → project playbook → specify…converge ✔ | agentic-sdd → playbook bug path → assess (how, why) → fix → converge → REA ✔ | skill-harness → poteto-mode Investigation → how → unslop ✔ |
| Cursor (no project rule) | `surgical-patch`/`cavecrew-builder` "or none" (mild over-pick) | agentic-sdd → playbook → sharpen → specify → how → plan+architect → tasks → implement poteto-agent+tdd → blast-radius → no-comments → converge+interrogate ✔ (read `agentic-sdd/SKILL.md`) | switched to Cursor plan mode and stalled on an interactive plan request; opened `diagnosing-bugs`, `investigate-first`, `agentic-sdd` (headless limit) | superpowers/caveman skills, no pstack, and a stale `jev_ask` line from an ai-memory global rule ✘ |
| Cursor (with `.cursor/rules/agentic-sdd.mdc`) | see rerun table below | – | see rerun | see rerun |
| Grok | none ✔ ("pstack mandate covers one-line edits directly") | skill-harness → agentic-sdd → phase map ✔ | poteto-mode Bug fix playbook + superpowers debugging, did **not** name agentic-sdd ✘ (project playbook not consulted). Rerun after `install.sh --grok-mandate` added the Spec Kit handoffs to the home rule (`tier1-grok-rule/`): agentic-sdd → bug stages `assess` (how, why, `assessment.md`) → `fix` (poteto Bug fix, `poteto-agent` leaf, tdd) → `test` (interrogate) → REA ✔ | poteto-mode Investigation → how → why → principles → unslop ✔ |

Findings:

1. No host over-invoked on the trivial task. The mandate's "smaller tasks, work
   directly" clause holds on all four.
2. The multi-file feature routed into Spec Kit phases on all four hosts, and all
   four kept poteto inside `O-poteto` instead of opening a free-standing playbook.
3. The bug and design cases separate hosts with a mandate from Cursor: Claude,
   Codex, and Grok reach pstack skills; Cursor without a project rule reaches
   other installed skill packs. Grok's bug answer skipped the project playbook.
4. A deleted ai-memory global rule (`_rules/agentic-sdd-jev-steer.md`) was still
   steering Cursor toward `jev_ask`; removed along with every other Jev artefact.
5. Cursor headless cannot answer a "plan" prompt that triggers its plan mode.

## Tier 1 rerun, Cursor with the project rule

Same prompts in the sandbox after `install.sh --project` wrote
`.cursor/rules/agentic-sdd.mdc` (`tier1-cursor-rule/`).

| Case | Before the rule | With the rule |
|---|---|---|
| T | `surgical-patch`/`cavecrew-builder` or none | `agentic-sdd; surgical-patch`, "no Spec Kit/pstack cycle" (over-pick: the typo sits in `specs/001-*`, and the rule's "names a numbered feature" trigger fired). The rule now carries a one-file exemption line. |
| B | stalled in plan mode, named only agentic-sdd | agentic-sdd → bug path `assess` (sharpen, how, why, repro) → `fix` (poteto-mode read as reference, Bug fix steps, tdd, architect if boundary) → `test` (interrogate, blast-radius, no-comments) → REA → PR only on policy ✔; explicitly "jev_* 없음" |
| D | superpowers/caveman skills + stale `jev_ask` | agentic-sdd read-only assessment → sharpen → how → specify/plan → architect/arena → blast-radius; poteto-mode read, not invoked ✔ |

The project rule closes the Cursor gap for bug and design routing. The
remaining Cursor-specific limit is that `poteto-mode` itself can only be opened
by the user.

## Tier 2, real feature end to end

One prompt, four hosts, same base clone: deliver `todo edit <id> <new text>` as
a new numbered feature through agentic-sdd, Economy mode, converge once, REA
closeout, unattended. Measured by `measure_tier2.py` (files + transcript).

| Measure | Claude Code | Codex (`gpt-6-luna`) | Cursor (`composer`) | Grok |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| New spec | `002-todo-edit`, 4 tasks done | `002-todo-edit`, 3 tasks done | `002-todo-edit`, 3 tasks done | `002-todo-edit`, 5 tasks done |
| Black-box: edit works / list shows new text / unknown id fails | ✔ ✔ ✔ | ✔ ✔ ✔ | ✔ ✔ ✔ | ✔ ✔ ✔ |
| Own tests | OK (18) | OK | OK (18) | OK (17) |
| Converge count | 1 (T004 appended from interrogate, implemented, **no second converge**) | 1 (zero findings, criterion gate `advance=true`) | 1 (T003 appended, implemented, no second converge) | 1 (converged, zero findings; "Do not run converge again" recorded) |
| REA Evidence | `ev_d529d796…` pass (MCP 6.7.0) | 3 ids (`ev_176462a0…`, `ev_96797c5c…`, `ev_a46d7dc9…`) in `converge.md` + `evidence/rea.json` | `ev_7c5263c4…` pass (MCP) | `ev_145d76d8…` pass (MCP) + 3 more ids in the bundle |
| Breadcrumbs added | `harness:`, `pstack: hook-mandate`, O-sharpen, O-specify, O-how, O-architect n/a, O-sequence, `ROUTING:`, O-poteto ×2, O-blast, O-hygiene, O-interrogate ×2, O-rea, O-reflect skipped | prose bullets per obligation (Skill gate, Harness, Specify, O-hygiene, O-blast, O-interrogate, Converge, criterion gate, O-rea); no `pstack:` prefix form | `pstack: 0.15.28`, `harness:` all ok, O-sharpen…O-rea, `ROUTING:` ×2 | full line form: `pstack: 0.9.93|grok`, `harness:`, O-sharpen, O-specify (technical-writing + unslop), O-how (poteto-agent explainer), O-architect (2 poteto-agent runners), O-sequence, O-poteto (worktree leaf), O-blast, O-interrogate (2 reviewers), O-converge, O-rea, `ROUTING:` ×3 |
| Implement leaf | `pstack:poteto-agent-low` on `sonnet` in a worktree, cherry-picked by the lead | `spawn_agent` delegates (35 dispatch events); native `reviewer` role rejected `gpt-6.1-sol` under the ChatGPT account, fell back to a general read-only agent | `poteto-agent` dispatch **failed on usage limit**; parent implemented locally and recorded `observed: unavailable` | `spawn_subagent` `poteto-agent` in a worktree (T002–T004), parent copied the diff and verified; model unpinned (no Grok sheet), observed unknown |
| Review | 2× `pstack:effort-low` (opus, haiku) → 1 act-on | 2 reviewers requested `gpt-6-luna@low` and `gpt-5.6-terra@low`, observed unknown | 2 seats, both `inherit` (second family unavailable on limit) → 1 act-on | 2 reviewer subagents, no findings |
| Commits added / dirty | 6 / 0 | 10 / 0 | 9 / 0 | 6 / 1 (untracked `decisions.tsv`) |
| Wall / cost | 519 s, $7.49, 11 top-level turns | 582 s (subscription) | 521 s (subscription) | 1997 s, $7.15, 77 turns (grok-4.7-build) |

Observations:

1. All four hosts delivered the feature with a passing black-box check, exactly
   one converge, a REA Evidence id, and a resumable `progress.md`. The
   one-converge rule held on every host: the act-on item from interrogate was
   appended to `tasks.md` and implemented without a second converge.
2. Routing breadcrumbs differ in shape. Claude and Cursor use the `pstack:` /
   `ROUTING:` line form; Codex wrote prose bullets. The probe's L7 check and
   `measure.py` only count the line form, so the Codex phase contract should
   name the line form explicitly (fixed below).
3. Codex's `AGENTS.md` native role table still pins `gpt-6.1-sol` / Astra,
   which the ChatGPT-account `spawn_agent` rejects; the pstack sheet
   (`gpt-6-luna`) is what made dispatch work. One reviewer seat was requested as
   `gpt-5.6-terra`, a model the user excluded; the sheet must pin the panel.
4. Cursor's Agent CLI hit its usage limit mid-run; the skill degraded correctly
   (parent implemented, `observed: unavailable|usage-limit`, review seats
   recorded as `inherit`) instead of claiming a dispatch.
5. Economy mode behaved as written: `O-architect` marked n/a for a single-file
   change, two-reviewer panel, `technical-writing`/`unslop` as inline obligations.

Cursor rerun alone (`tier2-cursor-rerun/`, fresh clone, nothing else on the
Cursor account): same outcome, 453 s, 5 tasks, one converge (T004 appended),
REA `ev_35fc5c18…` pass, black-box ✔, and still `non-inherit second family
unavailable (usage limit)`. So the limit is the account's standing state for
non-default model seats, not a parallel-run artefact; the degradation path
(parent-implemented leaf, `inherit` review seats, recorded as such) is what the
skill does under it. Grok ran with no `pstack-models.md`
sheet, so every `ROUTING:` line reads `model unpinned, observed unknown` (L6 is
defaults-only on Grok until `/setup-pstack` writes a sheet). Commit counts are
commits after the shared base `3ff57a9`, excluding the Cursor rule commit.

## Tier 3, complex goal with the split rule (all hosts)

Prompt: priorities, due dates, `list --sort due|priority`, `list --overdue`,
migration of existing stores, tests; Economy; split when tasks exceed ~12;
carryover instead of reconverge. Same black-box script on every result:
`add --priority 1 --due …`, invalid priority rejected, `--sort due`,
`--sort priority`, `--overdue`, legacy store entry preserved.

| Measure | Claude Code | Codex | Cursor | Grok |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Specs | `002-priority-due` (8) → `003-sort-overdue` (6); split up front by dependency | one spec `002-todo-priority-dates`, 7 tasks ("below the 12-task threshold"); no split | `002-priority-due` (7) → `003-sort-overdue` (5); split 002/003 | `002-add-priority` (7) → `003-add-due-date` (7) → `004-list-sort` (7); three specs declared up front |
| Converge per spec | 1 + 1, each appended one interrogate task; no reconverge | 1 | 1 + 1 | 1 + 1 + 1 |
| REA | `ev_ae808042…`, `ev_3ee0707c…` pass | `ev_064ed609…`, `ev_4e85e0ee…` pass | `ev_fafe77f2…`, `ev_18de17b2…` pass | `ev_b505f7e4…`, `ev_ac1063c2…`, `ev_05bd7810…` pass |
| Tests / `todo` lines | 28 OK / 110 | OK / 116 | OK / 131 | OK / 141 |
| Black-box | all ✔ (invalid input exit 2) | all ✔ (legacy item shown as `[P3]`: migration fills a default priority, text kept) | all ✔ (invalid priority exit 1) | all ✔ (legacy item shown as `p3`; `--sort priority` ties broken by id) |
| Carryover | none needed | none needed | none needed | none needed |
| Wall / cost | 1151 s, $12.07 | 643 s | 426 s (leaf `unavailable|usage-limit`, parent implemented) | 5113 s, $17.65, 123 turns |

The split rule produced different but valid shapes: Claude and Cursor split by
dependency into two specs, Codex kept one 7-task spec, Grok planned three. The
one-converge rule held everywhere, and no host needed a carryover spec because
the single fix round closed every interrogate finding.

## Cursor `/poteto-mode` under agentic-sdd

`agent -p "/poteto-mode <feature, plan only>"` in the base sandbox with the
project rule installed (`tier1-cursor-rule/cursor-slash-poteto.jsonl`): the
session opened `agentic-sdd/SKILL.md` and the Feature playbook, judged that 001
is closed and `edit` needs a new numbered feature, listed the Spec Kit phases
with their obligations (sharpen → how → specify → plan+architect → tasks →
implement as `O-poteto` with `poteto-agent` leaves → blast/no-comments →
converge+interrogate → REA), and stated it would not open a free-standing
Feature todolist. The user-invoked path hands off to Spec Kit as designed.

## Judgment

**Does agentic-sdd + pstack + the seven layers produce synergy on every host?**
Yes on all four hosts for the real feature, with measurable evidence (black-box
pass, one converge, REA Evidence, breadcrumbs), and yes for proportional
routing on the four plan-only prompts. The parts reinforce each other in a specific way:

- Spec Kit supplies the phase order and the artifacts (L2 procedure, L7 goal);
  pstack supplies the per-phase rigor (how/architect/interrogate/poteto leaves,
  L5 reviewer evidence, L6 effort routing); the harness probe and `progress.md`
  breadcrumbs make the whole thing resumable and auditable (L1, L7). Where one
  layer was missing the others compensated visibly: Cursor's dispatch limit
  degraded to a recorded parent-implemented leaf, Codex's untrusted hook was
  replaced by the AGENTS.md mandate, the REA closeout caught nothing on these
  small features but ran on every host with real Evidence ids.
- Invocation is proportional. The trivial task invoked nothing on all four
  hosts; the feature invoked the full phase map; the bug and the design question
  routed to assess/investigate paths without implementing.
- Cost is the price: $7.49 for a 30-line feature on Claude (Economy, 2
  reviewers), $12.07 for the two-spec Tier 3. Subscription hosts hide the
  dollar figure but spent 7–33 minutes of wall time per feature. On the same
  Tier 3 brief, wall time ran about 1× (Claude, Cursor) / 0.6× (Codex, one spec)
  / 4.4× (Grok, three specs, $17.65, 123 turns, 184k-token context at the end).
  Every extra spec pays the full phase overhead (probe, sharpen, how, specify,
  plan, tasks, converge, REA), so "keep specs small" trades per-spec context
  size for more fixed cost; the split should follow dependencies, not a count.

What this run changed in the skill: `install.sh --codex-mandate` (mandate block
in `~/.codex/AGENTS.md`); `--grok-mandate` now appends the three Spec Kit
handoffs; Cursor project rule template and `--project` installer step;
`poteto-mode-anatomy.md`; the breadcrumb line-form contract made explicit for
Codex; GPT-5.6 exclusion written into the Codex sheet; the stale Jev global
memory rule deleted; raw headless transcripts gitignored (`*.jsonl`, `*.err`).

Not exercised: Cursor with a non-default model seat available (account usage
limit throughout this day); Codex `/hooks`-trusted plugin hook (the AGENTS.md
block covers it); REA on a compiled artifact (all runs were source-only
scripts captured with `capture_process_scenario`).

<!-- file: docs/evals/2026-10-20-host-matrix/prediction.md -->

# Host matrix: does agentic-sdd + pstack + the seven layers fire correctly on every host?

Written before any run. Judged from transcripts and files, never from the agent's own summary.

## Setup

- Base project: the `001-todo-cli` sandbox from `2026-10-19-sandbox-ab` (Spec Kit 1.0.1, feature 001 closed, `.agents/playbooks/agentic-sdd.md` installed, `progress.md` with breadcrumbs). One clone per host under the scratchpad `hm/<host>/`.
- Hosts and headless drivers: Claude Code `claude -p --output-format stream-json`, Codex `codex exec --json -m gpt-6-luna`, Cursor `agent -p --output-format stream-json --force`, Grok `grok -p --always-approve --output-format json`.
- Entry directions tested: (a) explicit `/agentic-sdd` style request, (b) a plain request in a Spec Kit repo that the pstack mandate should route through poteto-mode and the project playbook.

## Tiers

| Tier | What | Cost | Pass condition |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 static | `harness_probe.py` per host; `check-playbooks.mjs` on the port; Cursor plugin playbook text vs the port | none | probe L2/L3/L5/L6 ok on all hosts; port validates; Cursor divergence documented |
| 1 routing | four "plan only, name the skills you would run, then stop" prompts per host: T (typo), F (multi-file feature), B (unknown bug), D (design question) | small | T: no poteto-mode, no agentic-sdd. F: agentic-sdd + Spec Kit phase named + poteto Feature steps. B: bug workflow + `how`/`why`. D: investigation/`how`/`architect`, no implement |
| 2 feature | one real small feature (`todo edit`) end to end on each host that can run unattended | moderate | files: new `specs/002-*`, `progress.md` gains `pstack:`/`harness:`/`ROUTING:` lines, one converge, REA Evidence id; transcript: poteto agent dispatch, review skill run |
| 3 split | Claude only: a change sized to exceed ~12 tasks (priorities + due dates + filter + store migration) | high | `closed-carryover` recorded and a smaller next spec specified, no second converge |

## Predictions

1. Tier 0: all four hosts L2 ok. Cursor's official plugin (0.15.28) has no project-playbook support and marks poteto-mode `disable-model-invocation: true`, so on Cursor the handoff relies on the agentic-sdd skill text, not the playbook.
2. Tier 1 T: every host answers without naming poteto-mode or agentic-sdd. Risk: Claude over-invokes because the mandate is injected every session.
3. Tier 1 F: Claude, Codex, Grok name agentic-sdd and the Spec Kit `specify` phase. Cursor names poteto-mode Feature steps but may miss the Spec Kit handoff unless it opens the agentic-sdd skill.
4. Tier 1 B: all hosts name a reproduce-first bug flow; Claude and Codex name `how`/`why`.
5. Tier 2: Claude completes with Evidence. Codex completes if `spawn_agent` is given `gpt-6-luna`. Grok completes with `poteto-agent`. Cursor may stop at a question or skip REA.
6. Tier 3: Claude records carryover rather than reconverging.

<!-- file: docs/evals/2026-10-19-sandbox-ab/result.md -->

# A/B result: Spec Kit alone (A) vs agentic-sdd + pstack + harness layers (B)

Same brief (`todo` CLI, AC-1..AC-5, <200 LOC), same Spec Kit 1.0.1 scaffold,
same model (opus, headless `claude -p`, bypassPermissions). B started before
the one-converge-per-spec rule landed, so its two converge rounds reflect the
old policy.

| Metric (measured) | A | B |
|---|---|---|
| Black-box AC-1..AC-4 (measure.py) | all pass | all pass |
| Own test suite | 6 tests, OK | 15 tests, OK |
| Corrupt store (`{"oops":1}`) | Python traceback | `todo: cannot read …: not a todo store`, exit 1 |
| Unwritable path | traceback | `todo: cannot write …`, exit 1 |
| `done abc` | "no item with id abc" (string compare) | argparse int error |
| Implementation LOC | 63 (`todo.py` + 8-line `todo` shim) | 80 (`todo`) |
| Spec artifacts | spec/plan/tasks/research/data-model/contracts/quickstart | same + `converge.md` |
| progress.md | none | 8 sections, Next action, 16 breadcrumbs, ROUTING line |
| Independent review | none | interrogate 4 models → 4 act-on → T011–T014; blast-radius level-4 proof; re-review by a second model |
| REA closeout | not attempted | attempted twice, `blocked-limitation` (host CLT modulemap defect), feature left open |
| Commits | 3 | 8 |
| Turns / wall / cost | 21 / 135 s / $0.96 | 24 / 582 s / $11.24 |

## Failure probes (verbatim)

```text
== A corrupt store
TypeError: string indices must be integers, not 'str'   (traceback, rc=1)
== A unwritable dir
FileNotFoundError: [Errno 2] No such file or directory: '/nonexistent/dir/todo.json'   (traceback)
== A done non-int
todo: no item with id abc
== B corrupt store
todo: cannot read _bad.json: not a todo store   (rc=1)
== B unwritable dir
todo: cannot write /nonexistent/dir/todo.json: [Errno 2] No such file or directory: '/nonexistent/dir/todo.json.tmp'
== B done non-int
todo done: error: argument id: invalid int value: 'abc'
```

## Against the pre-registered prediction

- Row 2 (independent review recorded): B won in this run. Four-model interrogate produced
  real defects (unvalidated store shape, write errors as tracebacks, file mode
  regression) that A shipped.
- Row 3 (resumable progress): B won in this run. A has no progress.md; B's `Next action`
  names the exact REA rerun.
- Row 6 (black-box parity or better): parity on AC-1..4; B strictly better on
  the three failure probes.
- Row 5 (scope control): both stayed inside AC; B added robustness, not
  features; both under 200 LOC.
- Cost: B is 11.7× the dollars and 4.3× the wall time of A. Prediction said
  2–4×; the panel (4 reviewers + re-review + 2 poteto leaves) is the cost.
- REA: B spent effort on a closeout that the host could not run. Correct per
  the rules (blocked-limitation, not finish), but zero evidence returned.

## Limits of this run

n = 1 per arm on one 60-line task. The prompts were asymmetric: B's prompt
named every obligation (`harness_probe`, `pstack:sharpen`, `how`, `architect`,
`poteto-agent`, `blast-radius`, `no-comments`, `interrogate`, breadcrumbs,
`ROUTING:`), while A's said only "use the speckit skills, no pstack". So the
run shows that the obligations, when executed, catch defects A shipped; it does
not show that `/agentic-sdd` alone triggers all of them unprompted. B's own
breadcrumb `O-specify … obligation-only` shows one Required row was skipped
even when prompted. Failure probes below are the load-bearing evidence.

## Judgment

Effective for SDD: **yes, on correctness evidence and continuity; no, on cost
for a task this small.** The stack found and fixed three defects A shipped,
left an auditable trail, and never claimed finish without REA. For a 60-line
feature that is $10 of insurance. The value claim scales with feature size and
risk: the per-feature fixed cost (probe, sharpen, how, architect, interrogate,
REA) is roughly constant while the defects it catches grow with surface area.

## What this run tells us to change

1. Cost tiering: `cost-modes.md` Economy/Balanced should shrink the interrogate
   panel (2 reviewers) and skip `architect` for single-file specs; Thorough
   keeps the full panel. Already partly expressed; make it explicit per
   obligation.
2. REA on a plain Python script: `open_binary` is unsupported and
   `capture_process_scenario` depends on host toolchain. Document the
   `not-applicable` path for source-only CLIs with no build artifact, so a
   healthy host is not blocked by a tooling gap it cannot fix.
3. One-converge rule (now landed) would have cut B's second converge; the
   re-review would still run as "affected checks".

## Host-fix follow-up (after the measured run)

The table above is the experiment. These checks ran later, on 2026-10-19,
after Command Line Tools 26.6.0.0.1781586589 replaced CLT 16.4. They do not
change the A/B cost or the original `blocked-limitation`.

- `xcrun swiftc` of `rea-agents` `bridge/process/ProcessRunTokenReader*.swift` exits 0. The 2023 `usr/include/swift/module.modulemap` is still on disk; this compiler no longer reports `redefinition of module 'SwiftBridging'`.
- Fresh CLI `npx -y rea-agents@6.4.0 capture-process` on arm B's `./todo` scenario: `ev_500769f77dcd683a767e00aca8fa1517a60f62f73ed46be8eff22ff1d718cbdb`, exit 0, cleanup `owned_process_group: verified`. Terminal shows add/list/done and the JSON store.
- Cursor MCP `capture_process_scenario` on `/usr/bin/true`: `ev_b9bcb0045959c76f93729a5fc0e892f26bbb385fc25df87eb55e347a4b65fe2e`, exit 0, cleanup verified.
- Same MCP on the arm B `./todo` scenario: `ev_7dc83a232e62fc41354807e92a2f66d5e89a90360e9c7fc511a47e1578e02aa1`, exit 0. Rendered lines include `1 buy milk`, `2 write report`, `rc=0`, `todo: no item with id 99`, `rc=1`, and the store with id 1 done. Disposition for this rerun: `pass`. No material finding.
- 2026-10-20 follow-up: this Claude session's MCP server (rea-agents 6.4.0, started before the CLT update) kept failing with `cleanup_incomplete … environment_unavailable` after reconnect. The live candidates were Chrome Helper (Renderer) processes (`csops` flags: `CS_RESTRICT` set, not platform binaries) spawned during the capture; 6.4.0 fails closed on them. Concurrent 14 s captures of `/bin/sleep` while tabs opened and closed: 6.4.0 rc=1 (`environment_unavailable=2`), 6.7.0 rc=0, `ev_92225e1401e61b2d0a4132e82caf8d7343d2b15617f7347a8a66b46eb41f027d`, cleanup verified, those PIDs recorded as `restricted_process_environment_withheld`. All four host configs now pin 6.7.0.
- Lesson 1 is in the panel-size table in `references/pstack-integration.md` (Economy: skip single-file architect, 2 reviewers).
- Lesson 2 stays `blocked-limitation` when the capture helper cannot compile. A source-only script is not `not-applicable`; it uses `capture_process_scenario`. A healthy host now returns Evidence.

Host checks from the same night, outside the A/B cost:

- Codex has no `/goal` (`codex --help`). `spawn_agent` with `model=gpt-6-luna` and `reasoning_effort=low` started; the child replied OK. Omitting the model is still rejected as `gpt-6.1-sol`.
- Cursor CLI `agent -p` can open the linked `poteto-mode` skill by path. It does not list that skill in the session catalog.
- Grok `spawn_subagent` enum includes user agent `poteto-agent`. `grok models` (logged in) lists `grok-4.7`, `grok-4.7-build-fast`, `grok-4.6`, `grok-4.5`. The pstack SessionStart script is not executed; the mandate is the home rule.
- `install.sh --apply-cursor-hooks` and `--uninstall` were run against a temporary HOME. Uninstall removes the continuation hooks and leaves unrelated hooks. The live `~/.cursor/hooks.json` entries stayed. `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests` → 90 tests OK.
- `git init` in this skill directory. No commit.
